name: Congressman Vince Fong
subject: Fighting for Affordability
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vince Fong for Congress
body:
Something I am hearing every day in California: the cost of living is crushing families here. | | |
---
| |
# Fighting for Affordability
---
| Friend, Something I am hearing every day in California: the cost of living is crushing families here. Ask anyone in our district what worries them most, and the high cost of living tops the list. I’ve been fighting for more affordability in California since my first day in Sacramento and I’ve continued that fight in Washington, DC. Back [in 2020, when I introduced legislation to cut taxes](https://us.list-manage.com/13yMt3dNpaz?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) for middle class families, small businesses, and renters, I said plainly: _"The cost of living in California is driving out so many families to other states because they cannot bear this burden any longer."_ That same year, [I called out Sacramento](https://us.list-manage.com/4jGYZDROlMJ?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) for quietly hiking the gas tax by another $440 million without so much as a vote of the Legislature or the public. By [2022, with inflation hammering household budgets](https://us.list-manage.com/wekW4nxiB76?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) and gas topping $5.70 a gallon in parts of our state, I was back at it again, introducing legislation to suspend the state gas tax outright. Something is wrong in California when the average price of gasoline in our state is $6.21 and the average price in Indiana is $3.89. We know one of the first things our out of state friends do while visiting is they take a photo of California’s gas prices. I've been fighting this fight since I first got to the State Assembly in 2016, long before affordability became the issue everyone's suddenly talking about. It's why I've spent my time in Congress fighting Sacramento's hidden climate tax on shipping that drives up prices at the register and the pump. It's why I fought to pull the plug on California's $128 billion high-speed rail boondoggle instead of letting it drain resources from roads and water systems that actually serve our families. It's why I'm fighting the State Water Board every time it tries to raise costs and uncertainty for the farmers who feed this country. It’s why I am working to expand oil and gas production in our community, to invest in California’s energy pipeline infrastructure, and to actually build and expand refining capacity to support increase supplies of needed gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. I will continue to work every single day to tackle the affordability crisis in California. Let’s invest in water infrastructure to increase needed water supplies for our homes, businesses and farms. Let’s increase California’s gasoline and diesel supplies to lower prices at the pump. Let’s get rid of red tape and bureaucracy that is making everything more expensive. And let’s reduce your tax burden so you keep more of your hard earned money. Thank you for standing with me,
Congressman Vince Fong

The numbers look good. Here’s why I’m not taking a victory lap.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141740770/654587184/-1038038363?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_NF_Briefing2_261005_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTgzYjc2M2UtZDhjYi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=DnWC9zWvEvBmizlo7pqyE_f5UmfRnWJyMeSH6ApRwLE=&emci=e203d2a6-cccb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=e83b763e-d8cb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=17458827)
Peter,

I want to give you an update on what I’m seeing as chair of the Democratic Governors’ Association and in my conversations with candidates and voters as I’m traveling the country for campaign stops:

Democrats are doing well in the polls. Folks are tired of rising costs and ready for leaders who will focus on their families. I’m encouraged by that.

But I know a thing or two about tough races. I’ve won three times statewide in a state Donald Trump carried by more than 30 points, and I can tell you that a poll is a snapshot, not a result. Nobody gets a trophy for being ahead with two weeks to go. You run through the tape.

That’s why In This Together is running ads and making direct contributions to candidates in tough races. This election is absolutely critical for the future of our country, and we have to compete in as many places as possible.

Here are just a few of the things at stake:

Diesel hit an all-time high last month, and it’s still above six dollars a gallon. Gas is more than a dollar higher than it was a year ago. That’s going to raise the cost of transporting groceries, building materials and just about everything else you buy. Donald Trump’s war with Iran has driven those prices up, and working families are the ones paying for it.

Back home in Kentucky, we’re dealing with the highest number of measles cases in 35 years. Diseases we had virtually eliminated are coming back because of bad public health advice and a Secretary of Health and Human Services, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who isn’t qualified to be giving it.

And there’s something else weighing on me this week. More than 80,000 Kentuckians have lost access to SNAP benefits because of the Trump administration’s cuts, and they’re now at risk of going hungry. So last week, I sent a letter to the Trump administration asking them to take action. Nobody should have to wonder where their next meal is coming from.

My faith teaches me to love my neighbor, and everyone is my neighbor. Right now, a lot of our neighbors are getting squeezed, and they deserve leaders who show up for them.

So here’s what I’m asking of you. Make a plan to vote. Check on a neighbor who might not. Talk to the friend who’s sitting this one out. If you’ve got an hour to spare, go knock some doors for a candidate you believe in. And as always, please reply with your thoughts about this election – I’d love to hear from you.

Let’s run through the tape together.

Thank you for all you do.

Andy

Join us for a community call and start organizing! | | | Peter, This administration’s mass delegalization agenda didn’t slow down. It just got harder to see. In July, federal immigration agents made nearly 51,000 arrests, a record high. And they're doing it faster and quieter than ever. People are being detained while taking out the trash, pumping gas, driving to work, and at the airport. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpw9l-ngjXclNoM0Ou8ZiAaIE1OF_xDI2niJbM2MS9qEr46VmGhJKSYFLbW3lXcl5FUJw1q1QM1mIj3xmkRXtB3M9TSvHNFHC-xHvrULAcvX2z2e1i8p7CeeO_-TjYYp_T9Os0dmRzaZSBoYtKPR6mKeYbVBGpUUsv0zpiIs-PJ7IvLK_JYIRNlZxQBFaXXzvIdpegoGkb43YRLze_uA0RP-qMLwenP7apxnCZOZagejED0V47IWag2blF3KiFKSs4/4v0/C9Y5ovkxTZyBeybhus5pyQ/h0/h001.pURnbE2pPSaU-NDl3SR0j3XWgXx03ReraSIG8ODM7_Q) It’s not just federal agents anymore. As of September, ICE has signed more than 2,500 agreements that also let local police and sheriffs carry out immigration enforcement. Families are being torn apart, and people are being kept in detention; permanent citizenship is the only solution.

In July, federal immigration agents made nearly 51,000 arrests, a record high. And they're doing it faster and quieter than ever. People are being detained while taking out the trash, pumping gas, driving to work, and at the airport. It’s not just federal agents anymore. As of September, ICE has signed more than 2,500 agreements that also let local police and sheriffs carry out immigration enforcement. Families are being torn apart, and people are being kept in detention; permanent citizenship is the only solution. Organizing people and coming together is how we're going to keep each other safe and how we're going to win a pathway to citizenship. . Speakers emphasized the importance of fighting back against antisemitism in all its forms and highlighted Cait Conley as the candidate who will best support and defend the Jewish community — here in the Hudson Valley and across the country. “As antisemitism rises at alarming rates in New York and across the country, today is about standing in solidarity with our Jewish neighbors, and demonstrating that hate has no place in the Hudson Valley. It is incumbent upon all of us — especially our elected leaders — to fight back against antisemitism in all its forms and never fuel it. I will always be committed to ensuring that our Jewish community members feel safe and welcome here, and I’m incredibly grateful for the support of groups like the Westchester Jewish Democrats and the Jewish Democratic Council of America, ” said **Cait Conley, Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District.** “To have a candidate during these times we know we can count on to stand strong with our community is incredible. It is so important right now for Jewish Democrats broadly, and certainly here in NY-17. Let’s go out and get this done for Cait Conley,” said **Nancy Street, Chair of the Westchester Jewish Democrats.** “NY-17 has the largest Jewish voting population of any of the vitally important red-to-blue congressional districts in the country, with Jewish Americans making up nearly one-fifth of its population. We're proud to support veteran Cait Conley in this race, and are confident a majority of Jewish voters in the district will vote for her because she aligns with our values,” said **Halie Soifer, CEO of the Jewish Democratic Council of America.** **** **** ### **About Cait Conley** Cait Conley is a Hudson Valley native, the daughter of a postal worker and a construction worker. She applied to West Point the day after 9/11 and went on to serve in the Army, first as a military police officer and then in special operations leadership, deploying six times and earning three Bronze Stars. Cait concluded her active-duty career as Director for Counterterrorism at the National Security Council, where Russia sanctioned her for her work, and then served as a senior executive at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, protecting critical infrastructure and the systems that run our elections. She put her life on the line to serve this country, not any person or political party, and especially not corporate special interests. Now, Cait is running to take on corruption so politicians can’t keep lining their pockets at the taxpayers’ expense, including by banning stock trading; lowering middle-class taxes; and holding monopoly utility companies and Big Pharma accountable to lower costs. Peter, we’re running out of time.
**President Trump is coming to North Carolina tomorrow** for his big MAGA rally with my opponent, Michael Whatley, and we need to hit our $1,000,000 goal before then. We can’t get there without grassroots support from people like you. [**_Please, will you chip in $5 or any amount right now to help us close the gap?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1702&amount=5&t=8&akid=4739%2E124072%2Ege4NqY)
I want to share three reasons why your $5 will make a huge difference for our campaign.
1\. If we lose in NC, Democrats lose our shot at taking back the Senate for the people. That’s why the GOP – including Trump’s own super PAC – has poured millions into this race to defeat me.
2\. In our state, winning a U.S. Senate race by a “landslide” means winning, at best, 51% of the vote and we haven’t elected a Democrat in almost two decades. That’s how competitive our elections are, no matter what the polls or pundits say.
3\. We’re falling short of our $1 million goal to respond to Trump’s oncoming attacks. If we’re caught flat-footed tomorrow, we could jeopardize our chances of flipping this seat.
Unlike Whatley, I don’t rely on megadonors to swoop in and save our campaign when we fall short. I fully depend on people like _you_ , Peter, chipping in what you can, when you can to power this grassroots movement forward.
**Right now, I need you with me.[_Will you please give $5 to help us close the gap on our crucial goal before Trump comes to North Carolina? It’s the only way we can keep up our momentum, win this race and take back the Senate._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1702&amount=5&t=9&akid=4739%2E124072%2Ege4NqY)**

By the time the public could buy shares, the biggest gains were often gone. Personal flight may be one of the first new industries where ordinary investors can get in on the ground floor. Connected file | | Everything Plugs Into the Same Grid ---|--- Electric cars, electric aircraft, heat pumps and AI data centers all draw on the same strained power system. The EIA expects the average U.S. home electricity price to rise about 5% this year, and in August the White House declared a national emergency over threats to America’s power grid. When more of your life plugs into the wall, having power when the grid fails matters more than ever. | | Sponsored by 4Patriots There's one mistake you never want to discover AFTER the power goes out: you didn't prepare with enough power. And with a FREE 200-Watt Solar Panel , you have a way to recharge it using the sun when ordinary electricity isn't available. Over 5 million Americans trust 4Patriots emergency products. | Why it matters to you | | Why Early Matters ---|--- | → | The legal path just opened. For the first time, there’s a category these aircraft can be certified in. ---|--- | → | Everyone understands the appeal. Anyone who’s sat in traffic gets it in seconds. ---|--- | → | The door is open before the listing. Some developers are offering shares to individuals now, with all the risk that involves. ---|--- | Classification Ground floor The flying car has been a promise for 70 years. What’s new is that the rules, the batteries and the funding model have all arrived at once. The earliest backers take the most risk, and have the most potential upside. Connected file | | What Electric Motors Are Made Of ---|--- Every electric motor, from a car to an aircraft, depends on materials like rare earths and lithium, and most of the world’s rare earth processing happens in China. That’s why Washington is so focused on new supplies. In September, President Trump signed a security agreement covering Greenland, an island with large rare earth deposits. But some of the most valuable deposits may be much closer to home. | | Sponsored by Stansberry Research Because this breakthrough new technology is unlocking hidden resources all across America. Government scientists from the Department of Energy used it to find $32 billion worth of rare earths at an old coal mine out in Wyoming. The Secretary of the Interior, Doug Burgum, says America is sitting on $200 trillion worth of natural resources. | | Open file · unresolved Who is building a flying car for your driveway? One developer is building a two-seat electric aircraft designed for vertical takeoff and home charging, and is offering individual investors shares before a potential public listing. body:
The same bureaucrat who shut Ohio down wants the Governor’s mansion.

| Peter,
The Left has a playbook: create panic, expand government power, then tell you it’s for your own good.
[Ohio saw that playbook during COVID. And the person who ran it is now the Democrats’ candidate for governor: Amy “Dr. Lockdown” Acton.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._MLRwCk3GZQ)
---
[](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
We will NEVER forget how she treated us.
Acton claimed 100,000 Ohioans were already infected, only to walk the number back within 24 hours. But the panic had already set in, and fear became the justification for sweeping government control.
Schools shut down across the state. Businesses had to fight the government in court just to survive. Families were told where they could go and how they could live.
[That wasn’t leadership. That was a bureaucratic takeover.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-CrI3vspRZNpiEV8bmjkOQ)
And now the same political kabal that pushed lockdowns wants to rewrite history and send Ohio’s Anthony Fauci to the Governor’s mansion.
And here’s the bigger truth: The same people who shut down Ohio also believe the government should control your economy. They use “equity” as a smokescreen to treat your private property like a government ATM. They create a crisis, and then demand you pay for it.
[Vivek is running for Governor of Ohio to build a firewall against that radicalism.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._hG0lcjmY-smx2w)
But we cannot be asleep at the wheel. The Democrat machine is flooding Ohio with money. And the latest poll shows Vivek is trailing by just ONE point.
[Peter, if you believe you — not the government — should be in charge of your life, help Vivek stop these tyrants in their tracks:](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-cs7SwMZQ)

ICE is going after people with no history of violent crime — targeting people at hospitals, airports, laundromats, and outside schools. It’s only October, and already I've heard countless stories of ICE targeting parents who are dropping their kids off at school, college students driving by campus, and children arriving home from school only to find their parents are gone. Right now, toddlers are being forced to represent themselves in immigration courts ([literally](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141745431/654597508/439072924?Date=20260929&Profile=CNN,CNN+Politics&utm_content=1790640182&utm_medium=social&utm_source=facebook&fbclid=IwY2xjawUz30RleHRuA2FlbQIxMABwZG9mBWJyaWQRMThEMUljUU5kcGFZbGhxU2FzcnRjBmFwcF9pZBAyMjIwMzkxNzg4MjAwODkyAAEeolapIl0pdhuSRBPoOcOAAX7ToirLc6qJLgezLFUgKIVzCzdBwn4wz64byIg_aem_6Tfeel70N-d7J0WWB62hYQ&refcode=261019em_sjj_ICE&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYThjNGQ4My1kZWNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lgiekGjGn9ToeCz74rATl2HsJ_THGCooDSd5g5SDcFM=&emci=9d139a10-c5c8-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=aa8c4d83-decb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=14239920)) and being deported when they fail to prove their asylum cases. The most interesting story in American immigration policy right now is not happening at the border. It's happening in white papers. Four of them, published over the past eighteen months, by four organizations that most Americans have never heard of, describing -- in sober, footnoted, foundation-funded prose -- a future in which the placement of immigrants into American towns becomes a designed, data-driven, privately administered process.
None of these documents became law. All of them are real. And read together, they sketch something that hasn't yet happened but now has a complete paper trail: a system for deciding which American communities receive newcomers -- and, just as notably, for deciding how those communities should feel about it.
Start with the concept.
**The concept: a visa for fading places**
In 2019, the Economic Innovation Group -- a Washington think tank co-founded by John Lettieri and, before he was vice president, J.D. Vance -- published a proposal called the Heartland Visa. The idea is elegantly simple: counties with chronic population loss could _opt in_ to a new visa category, recruiting high-skilled immigrants and entrepreneurs to settle specifically in them. Immigrants would get a pathway tied to staying; counties would get people; the interior would get the growth that has been flowing to the coasts for forty years.
EIG revived and expanded the idea in January 2025, proposing a floor of 100,000 visas a year, scalable to 500,000 depending on participation. It has never come close to enactment. It doesn't need to be enacted to matter -- because while EIG was supplying the concept, another organization was supplying everything else.
**The machinery: a blueprint and a matching engine...**

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
These incredible women leaders are fighting to build true progressive governing power.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261019-6856-footer&t=1&akid=6856%2E420207%2EhAc0Rd)
Peter,
We’re at crunch time, just 16 days before the election and these four fantastic women on the ballot need your help!
**Peggy Flanagan** for U.S. Senate, Minnesota
**Connie Chan** for U.S. House, CA-11
**Angie Nixon** for U.S. Senate, Florida
**Beth Macy** for U.S. House, VA-06
They’ve already spent their lives fighting for the people, against Big Money interests, and when we elect them, they will never back down from delivering for ALL of us.
These are courageous, people-powered fighters ready to work with our progressive coalition in Congress. They will help us finally pass Medicare for All, stand up to corporate power, and build a government that puts working families first — not the billionaires and special interests trying to buy our elections.
I’ve been campaigning on the ground with leaders across the country, and I know what these women are capable of when we support them.
I was just on the campaign trail with **Peggy** in Minnesota, where I stood alongside Elizabeth Warren rallying packed rooms of people ready to demand health care finally be treated as a human right. And when she wins, she’ll be the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate!
**Connie** pledged to co-sponsor my Medicare For All bill on day one — she is exactly the kind of committed and unapologetic fighter we need right now in the House. A proud immigrant just like me, she’ll join me as one of just two dozen naturalized citizens to serve in Congress when she wins a tight general election for the seat held by Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi for over 30 years.
I’ve watched as **Angie** has electrified Florida with her campaign for Medicare for All, universal childcare, a national rent freeze and moratorium on evictions, and stronger union protections. She wowed everyone by decisively winning the primary against a massively funded opponent, and now, for the first time in a long time, the US Senate seat for Florida is in play!
And I'm inspired every single day by **Beth’s** tireless work to expose the corporate greed behind the opioid epidemic. I knew of Beth Macy long before she ran for Congress, because she literally wrote the book that called out the role of Big Pharma in the spread of opioids that have killed so many millions across our country.
When these women win, we don’t just expand our governing power in Congress — we gain fierce organizers who aren’t afraid to challenge the status quo, stand up to Trump’s dangerous authoritarian agenda, and deliver for our communities.
**Right now, with 16 days left until Election Day, we need your support to make sure every one of these courageous leaders has the resources to organize and win.**[**If you’re able, will you split a donation between our campaigns to continue supporting Peggy, Connie, Angie, and Beth today?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261019-1.H3e0yS&refcode=em20261019-6856&amount=3&t=2&akid=6856%2E420207%2EhAc0Rd)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261019-1.H3e0yS&amount=3&refcode=em20261019-6856&t=21&akid=6856%2E420207%2EhAc0Rd)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

Dear Friend, We're just two weeks away from Election Day, and I have a personal request: **I need you to stand with me this Saturday.** On **Saturday, October 24** , we're holding a district-wide Rally Day, with supporters gathering across all six counties of Pennsylvania's 14th Congressional District. For months, I've traveled throughout southwestern Pennsylvania, listening to people who are frustrated with rising costs, worried about their healthcare, and tired of politicians who seem more interested in Washington than the people they're supposed to represent. I've heard you. And I'm ready to bring your voices to Congress. But I can't do this alone. **This Saturday, I want to see Bradstock supporters out in our communities, holding signs, showing their enthusiasm, and reminding their neighbors that we have a choice on November 3.** We've organized rally locations throughout the district, and I hope you'll join us at the one most convenient for you. **Most rallies will take place from 1 -3 PM.** Uniontown will be 11 AM-1 PM, and West Newton will begin at 5 PM.

Youssef Al-Sheikh in his home in the Jabaliya refugee camp in northern Gaza describes a raid by an Israel-backed Palestinian militia last month. September 26, 2026. Screenshot from video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
JABALIYA REFUGEE CAMP, Gaza Strip--Youssef Al-Sheikh was asleep with his wife and eight young children in a room on the ground floor of a badly damaged building in the wasteland of northern Gaza's Jabaliya refugee camp when the group of masked, heavily armed members of an Israeli-backed Palestinian militia broke down the door and stormed inside. It was around 2 a.m. on the night of September 24. Decked out in tactical gear and with their assault rifles pointing menacingly down at his family, they began shouting at Al-Sheikh to get up. The light from their military headlamps pierced the darkness, blinding Al-Sheikh.
"They came inside, and as soon as they entered, one of them raised his Kalashnikov and aimed it at me while I was here," Al-Sheikh told Drop Site News, pointing to the only bed in the room, made up of thin mattress laid on a thin piece of wood propped up on concrete blocks.
"About seven people came in. They all had flashlights on them--bright white lights, extremely powerful flashlights," he said. "With all the white light, I couldn't see who was in front of me."
The lead gunman started yelling "Qassam," Al-Sheikh said, a reference to the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades, the military wing of Hamas. "He said, 'Why are you staying here? Where are the explosive devices you have? Where are the weapons you have?'" Al-Sheikh recalled. "I told him, 'I'm a peaceful citizen. I don't have anything.'" When Al-Sheikh asked if could put some clothes on, the militiamen grabbed him and began savagely beating him in front of his wife and children.
"I couldn't process what was happening and didn't know what to do," Al-Sheikh said. "Three of them came at me, punching and slapping me and beating me. They beat me in the most brutal ways." Angry red bruises were still visible on his neck and back two days later.
They bound Al-Sheikh's hands behind his back and left him on the ground. Amid the commotion, one of Al-Sheikh's brothers-in-law entered from the room next door, pleading with the men to have mercy. "They grabbed him by his hair. Three of them attacked him, threw him to the ground, and beat him with their Kalashnikovs," Al-Sheikh said. When a second brother-in-law arrived, they also grabbed him and beat him with their rifle butts.
The militiamen took the three men into an adjacent room and made them kneel on the floor. What appeared to be the lead gunman pulled up a chair and sat in front of them. One of Al-Sheikh's brothers-in-law, Muatasim Al-Aja, had his hands bound and his mouth gagged. The other, Hossam Tafesh, also had his hands bound. The militiamen pulled out a black T-shirt from Tafesh's belongings and accused him of being a part of the resistance. When Tafesh said he had nothing to do with the resistance, they began beating him again and wrapped the T-shirt tightly around his face until he began to suffocate.
The other militiamen ransacked the rest of the house, going through and overturning the family's scant belongings and confiscating all the phones they could find. "One of my children was inside the room while this was happening and he started slapping himself. He's a little boy, a very young child," Al-Sheikh said. "He kept slapping himself across the face, crying, 'Dad, Dad, Dad! Where's my dad?' The officer told my wife, 'Either you shut the children up--all of you be quiet--or I'll shoot them all and kill them.'"
[](https://substack.com/redirect/29479b44-701b-4676-be8e-8be747a58f2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Youssef Al-Sheikh in his home in the Jabaliya refugee camp in northern Gaza that an Israel-backed Palestinian militia raided last month, beating him and his relatives and detaining one of them. September 26, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
Al-Sheikh said he later learned from eyewitnesses that an even larger militia force of close to 30 heavily armed men was surrounding the house outside. "It was as if an entire battalion had come to fight us," he said.
Eventually, the lead militiaman made Al-Sheikh and both of his brothers-in-law look into his phone camera and photographed their faces. "He photographed us and sent the pictures over WhatsApp," Al-Sheikh said. Several minutes later, the gunman received a call and announced they could be released.
At the same time, several gunmen went upstairs and detained a third brother-in-law, Said Okasha, who had gone up to the roof in fear. "They started beating him. We could hear the blows and the screaming. He was shouting, 'Leave me! Leave me!' They restrained him and took him away in his underwear," Al-Sheikh said. "They took him and left."
Two other residents in the area interviewed separately confirmed to Drop Site that a raid by a Palestinian militia had taken place that night.
## **" No One Comes to Help Us"**
Over the past year, since a "ceasefire" agreement went into effect, attacks by Israel-backed Palestinian militias have become increasingly frequent in Gaza, particularly targeting Palestinians living close to the "yellow line"--the demarcation of Israel's line of control that runs north to south along the Gaza Strip roughly parallel to the coastline. Israel has also imposed another boundary called the orange line, which in some places encroaches more than 1 kilometer beyond the yellow line, taking over even more Palestinian land.
On the western side of these lines, virtually the entire Palestinian population of Gaza has been corralled into an ever shrinking space. On the eastern side, the Israeli military has violently reconfigured the landscape, razing the area to the ground and building dozens of fortified bases and roads--establishing a permanent presence instead of preparing for a phased withdrawal as outlined in the ceasefire agreement.
Israeli forces regularly bomb, shell, and shoot Palestinians on the western side in violation of the "ceasefire," killing over 1,500 men, women, and children over the past 12 months. The Israeli military has also armed and equipped several Palestinian militias that operate on the ground, conducting raids and terrorizing people mostly living close to the yellow line. Large scale raids are conducted in coordination with the Israeli military, who have backed them up with artillery and aerial support.
Many of the militia leaders in Gaza who rose to power in collaboration with Israel during the genocide are former gang leaders with a history of criminal activity, were associated with jihadi groups, or are former Palestinian Authority security forces that were all sidelined after Hamas gained control of the enclave in 2007.
At least five of these militias are operating out of compounds in areas under Israeli military control across the Gaza Strip, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/bf8a311c-92ce-4ca6-8729-741fc44d89ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to satellite imagery and videos published online.
While Drop Site could not confirm which militia raided Al-Sheikh's house last month, the location of the building in the Jabaliya refugee camp is geographically closest to the northernmost militia compound in Gaza, located in Beit Hanoun, that is run by the Northern Forces, also known or the Popular Army. According to a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/3420f324-cd3d-48da-9e17-012b7e5c3190?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Al-Zaytouna Center for Consultations & Studies, the Northern Forces Forces/Popular Army was established in September 2025 and is led by Ashraf al-Mansi, who was previously accused of drug smuggling and other charges. The militia is made up of several dozen armed members and claims control over Jabaliya.
The building where Al-Sheikh and his family have been sheltering is next to the Jabaliya Services Club, a Palestinian sports club founded in the Jabaliya refugee camp by the UN Palestinian refugee agency--UNRWA--in the 1950s. The club was destroyed by Israeli occupation forces during the genocide and was briefly turned into a military barracks and interrogation center during Israel's ground invasion of Jabaliya in October 2024. Israeli forces eventually withdrew to the nearby yellow line following the ceasefire a year later.
Now, a few dozen displaced Palestinian families have sought shelter in and around the badly damaged sports club. The area has been turned into a gray moonscape through intense Israeli bombing and demolition, with mounds of rubble and destroyed buildings where a densely crowded urban landscape once stood. At the yellow line in the near distance, Israeli bases perched atop a massive earthen berm are clearly visible, with tall red and white communication towers protruding into the sky and a large Israeli flag billowing in the wind. Residents of the area describe a complete lack of food and water or any services, combined with frequent attacks by Israeli forces and collaborating Palestinian militias.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/138a3a1f-f61e-4d5f-8cc1-7f398100d7c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### The area near the Jabaliya Services Club in northern Gaza near the yellow line is completely destroyed with no access to food or water and frequently subject to attacks by Israeli forces and Palestinian militias. September 26, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
"There is basically no life here. We don't have enough water. There is indiscriminate gunfire 24 hours a day, as well as quadcopter fire and shelling. People are living with almost nothing," Ahmad Hammad, a displaced resident in the area told Drop Site. As he spoke, the crackle of machine gun fire punctuated the air. "As you can see, everything is rubble and debris. Rodents are everywhere. Heavy gunfire is almost a daily occurrence. It's a tragedy. No one comes to help us at all."
It is in areas like this in Gaza, close to the Israeli line of control, where Palestinian militias operate most frequently.
"Water trucks can't reach us, so we have to walk a long distance to get water," Safaa Al-Basyouni, a local resident, told Drop Site. "No food from charity kitchens reaches us at all. Shrapnel from Israeli fire falls around us. So we face danger from the Israelis, and on top of that, danger from the militias."
The majority of Palestinians in Gaza live in dense, squalid tent encampments that are infested with rodents and insects and provide little protection from the elements. Al-Basyouni and others came to the Jabaliya Services Club to try and find better shelter.
"We thought sheltering under concrete would be better than sheltering under a tent. That's what brought us here," she said. "But it was all for nothing. We still found insects here, and we found gunfire and shelling too. We don't know where to go. We came here hoping it would be better, but in reality, it turned out to be worse."
"Our situation here, so close to the yellow line, is tragic," Al-Basyouni continued. "We can't hide from the Israelis, and we can't hide from the militias."
While Israeli forces have taken to shooting, shelling, and bombing Palestinians from afar on a regular basis, the Palestinian militias are deployed to raid areas on the ground.
"The militias are constantly around here, and we're afraid of them. Suddenly, you find them surrounding the area with quadcopters, opening fire at us, and storming inside," Arafat Ali, who was displaced to the Jabaliya Services Club, told Drop Site. "Day and night, you find them coming in and attacking us. They recently beat four young men and detained one of them before leaving," he said, referring to the raid on Al-Sheikh's house. "Even the man they detained had nothing to do with any organization."
"We don't even understand how they operate. Suddenly, they open fire at us, fire shells, take young men captive, and then leave," Ali continued. "They don't come during the day. They come at three in the morning, like bandits."
There is no reliable count of how many people have been detained by Palestinian militias. Like many others, Said Okasha, Al-Sheikh's brother-in-law who was detained in the raid last month, is most likely imprisoned in one of Israel's detention camps where torture and abuse is systemic.
Meanwhile, Al-Sheikh himself has struggled to come to terms with the violence of the raid. "It was truly horrific--more horrific than you can imagine. Even now, speaking personally, apart from what this has done to my wife and children, what happened to me has left me hysterical and hallucinating. I walk down the street and tears start falling on their own," he said.
"No matter how much I describe the scene, I can't truly convey what it was like."
## **March of the Yellow Line**
The yellow line that Israeli troops initially withdrew to as part of the ceasefire agreement in October 2025 gave them control of 53% of the eastern side of the Gaza Strip, as outlined on Israel's own military maps. In some places, the line is demarcated by yellow concrete blocks, but in most of Gaza the boundary is invisible. Since then, Israeli forces have steadily pushed in, driving Palestinians further west, and expanding their control to close to 70% of the enclave.
Last week, Israeli troops moved further into Shujaiya, once a vast, densely populated neighborhood in eastern Gaza City. On October 11, displaced Palestinians who sought shelter in the area woke up to shooting and shelling by Israeli forces as they moved the yellow blocks some 200 meters further inward, sparking panic and another round of displacement.
"The yellow line used to be approximately 200 meters away from us. This morning, it was only 10 meters away," Osama Mushtaha, 50, told Drop Site.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a0835644-bd1e-40cd-b28c-6275622359fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Families in Shujaiya in eastern Gaza City are forced to flee following an attack by Israeli forces as they moved yellow blocks into the area, further expanding Israel's line of control. October 11, 2026. Video by Mohamed Ahmed.
Throughout the day, exhausted families gathered their scant belongings, piling mattresses and bags on the dusty streets, forced to flee once again in a desperate search for shelter.
"We're dying here every day because of the yellow line," Anis Herzallah, 30, said. "At night we have shelling, quadcopters, tanks, Apaches and F-16s--all of them attacking us from the yellow line. We can't live here anymore. "
The blocks in Shujaiya now lie close to Salah Al-Din street, a historic thoroughfare running north to south along the length of the Gaza Strip. Every encroachment of the yellow line brings Israel troops and the collaborating Palestinian militias ever closer.
"People are leaving, not knowing where they're supposed to go," a passerby said. "An Israeli tank and bulldozer advanced towards the area. They also have militias with them."
Sara Al-Ramlawi, 33, has been displaced with her family repeatedly over the past three years, moving from one place to another every few months before arriving at Shujaiya several months ago, only to be driven away yet again.
"We were forced out because they moved the yellow line closer, we have suffered so much," she told Drop Site. "We're heading into the unknown. This is our situation, and the situation of every family from Shujaiya living here."
"We're not asking for a house. Just a piece of land where we can put up tents."
_Mohamed Ahmed and Jawa Ahmad contributed to this report. Sami Vanderlip edited the video._

September 26, 2026. Screenshot from video by Abdel Qader Sabbah. JABALIYA REFUGEE CAMP, Gaza Strip--Youssef Al-Sheikh was asleep with his wife and eight young children in a room on the ground floor of a badly damaged building in the wasteland of northern Gaza's Jabaliya refugee camp when the group of masked, heavily armed members of an Israeli-backed Palestinian militia broke down the door and stormed inside. It was around 2 a.m. on the night of September 24. Decked out in tactical gear and with their assault rifles pointing menacingly down at his family, they began shouting at Al-Sheikh to get up. The light from their military headlamps pierced the darkness, blinding Al-Sheikh. "They came inside, and as soon as they entered, one of them raised his Kalashnikov and aimed it at me while I was here," Al-Sheikh told Drop Site News, pointing to the only bed in the room, made up of thin mattress laid on a thin piece of wood propped up on concrete blocks. "About seven people came in. They all had flashlights on them--bright white lights, extremely powerful flashlights," he said. "With all the white light, I couldn't see who was in front of me." The lead gunman started yelling "Qassam," Al-Sheikh said, a reference to the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades, the military wing of Hamas. "He said, 'Why are you staying here? Where are the explosive devices you have? Where are the weapons you have?'" Al-Sheikh recalled. "I told him, 'I'm a peaceful citizen. I don't have anything.'" When Al-Sheikh asked if could put some clothes on, the militiamen grabbed him and began savagely beating him in front of his wife and children. "I couldn't process what was happening and didn't know what to do," Al-Sheikh said. "Three of them came at me, punching and slapping me and beating me. They beat me in the most brutal ways." Angry red bruises were still visible on his neck and back two days later. They bound Al-Sheikh's hands behind his back and left him on the ground. Amid the commotion, one of Al-Sheikh's brothers-in-law entered from the room next door, pleading with the men to have mercy. "They grabbed him by his hair. Three of them attacked him, threw him to the ground, and beat him with their Kalashnikovs," Al-Sheikh said. When a second brother-in-law arrived, they also grabbed him and beat him with their rifle butts. The militiamen took the three men into an adjacent room and made them kneel on the floor. What appeared to be the lead gunman pulled up a chair and sat in front of them. One of Al-Sheikh's brothers-in-law, Muatasim Al-Aja, had his hands bound and his mouth gagged. The other, Hossam Tafesh, also had his hands bound. The militiamen pulled out a black T-shirt from Tafesh's belongings and accused him of being a part of the resistance. When Tafesh said he had nothing to do with the resistance, they began beating him again and wrapped the T-shirt tightly around his face until he began to suffocate. The other militiamen ransacked the rest of the house, going through and overturning the family's scant belongings and confiscating all the phones they could find. "One of my children was inside the room while this was happening and he started slapping himself. He's a little boy, a very young child," Al-Sheikh said. "He kept slapping himself across the face, crying, 'Dad, Dad, Dad! Where's my dad?' The officer told my wife, 'Either you shut the children up--all of you be quiet--or I'll shoot them all and kill them.'" Youssef Al-Sheikh in his home in the Jabaliya refugee camp in northern Gaza that an Israel-backed Palestinian militia raided last month, beating him and his relatives and detaining one of them. September 26, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah. Al-Sheikh said he later learned from eyewitnesses that an even larger militia force of close to 30 heavily armed men was surrounding the house outside. "It was as if an entire battalion had come to fight us," he said. Eventually, the lead militiaman made Al-Sheikh and both of his brothers-in-law look into his phone camera and photographed their faces. "He photographed us and sent the pictures over WhatsApp," Al-Sheikh said. Several minutes later, the gunman received a call and announced they could be released. At the same time, several gunmen went upstairs and detained a third brother-in-law, Said Okasha, who had gone up to the roof in fear. "They started beating him. We could hear the blows and the screaming. He was shouting, 'Leave me! Leave me!' They restrained him and took him away in his underwear," Al-Sheikh said. "They took him and left." Two other residents in the area interviewed separately confirmed to Drop Site that a raid by a Palestinian militia had taken place that night. " No One Comes to Help Us" Over the past year, since a "ceasefire" agreement went into effect, attacks by Israel-backed Palestinian militias have become increasingly frequent in Gaza, particularly targeting Palestinians living close to the "yellow line"--the demarcation of Israel's line of control that runs north to south along the Gaza Strip roughly parallel to the coastline. Israel has also imposed another boundary called the orange line, which in some places encroaches more than 1 kilometer beyond the yellow line, taking over even more Palestinian land. On the western side of these lines, virtually the entire Palestinian population of Gaza has been corralled into an ever shrinking space. On the eastern side, the Israeli military has violently reconfigured the landscape, razing the area to the ground and building dozens of fortified bases and roads--establishing a permanent presence instead of preparing for a phased withdrawal as outlined in the ceasefire agreement. Israeli forces regularly bomb, shell, and shoot Palestinians on the western side in violation of the "ceasefire," killing over 1,500 men, women, and children over the past 12 months. The Israeli military has also armed and equipped several Palestinian militias that operate on the ground, conducting raids and terrorizing people mostly living close to the yellow line. Large scale raids are conducted in coordination with the Israeli military, who have backed them up with artillery and aerial support. Many of the militia leaders in Gaza who rose to power in collaboration with Israel during the genocide are former gang leaders with a history of criminal activity, were associated with jihadi groups, or are former Palestinian Authority security forces that were all sidelined after Hamas gained control of the enclave in 2007. At least five of these militias are operating out of compounds in areas under Israeli military control across the Gaza Strip, to satellite imagery and videos published online. While Drop Site could not confirm which militia raided Al-Sheikh's house last month, the location of the building in the Jabaliya refugee camp is geographically closest to the northernmost militia compound in Gaza, located in Beit Hanoun, that is run by the Northern Forces, also known or the Popular Army. According to a by Al-Zaytouna Center for Consultations & Studies, the Northern Forces Forces/Popular Army was established in September 2025 and is led by Ashraf al-Mansi, who was previously accused of drug smuggling and other charges. The militia is made up of several dozen armed members and claims control over Jabaliya. The building where Al-Sheikh and his family have been sheltering is next to the Jabaliya Services Club, a Palestinian sports club founded in the Jabaliya refugee camp by the UN Palestinian refugee agency--UNRWA--in the 1950s. The club was destroyed by Israeli occupation forces during the genocide and was briefly turned into a military barracks and interrogation center during Israel's ground invasion of Jabaliya in October 2024. Israeli forces eventually withdrew to the nearby yellow line following the ceasefire a year later. Now, a few dozen displaced Palestinian families have sought shelter in and around the badly damaged sports club. The area has been turned into a gray moonscape through intense Israeli bombing and demolition, with mounds of rubble and destroyed buildings where a densely crowded urban landscape once stood. At the yellow line in the near distance, Israeli bases perched atop a massive earthen berm are clearly visible, with tall red and white communication towers protruding into the sky and a large Israeli flag billowing in the wind. Residents of the area describe a complete lack of food and water or any services, combined with frequent attacks by Israeli forces and collaborating Palestinian militias. The area near the Jabaliya Services Club in northern Gaza near the yellow line is completely destroyed with no access to food or water and frequently subject to attacks by Israeli forces and Palestinian militias. September 26, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah. "There is basically no life here. We don't have enough water. There is indiscriminate gunfire 24 hours a day, as well as quadcopter fire and shelling. People are living with almost nothing," Ahmad Hammad, a displaced resident in the area told Drop Site. As he spoke, the crackle of machine gun fire punctuated the air. "As you can see, everything is rubble and debris. Rodents are everywhere. Heavy gunfire is almost a daily occurrence. It's a tragedy. No one comes to help us at all." It is in areas like this in Gaza, close to the Israeli line of control, where Palestinian militias operate most frequently. "Water trucks can't reach us, so we have to walk a long distance to get water," Safaa Al-Basyouni, a local resident, told Drop Site. "No food from charity kitchens reaches us at all. Shrapnel from Israeli fire falls around us. So we face danger from the Israelis, and on top of that, danger from the militias." The majority of Palestinians in Gaza live in dense, squalid tent encampments that are infested with rodents and insects and provide little protection from the elements. Al-Basyouni and others came to the Jabaliya Services Club to try and find better shelter. "We thought sheltering under concrete would be better than sheltering under a tent. That's what brought us here," she said. "But it was all for nothing. We still found insects here, and we found gunfire and shelling too. We don't know where to go. We came here hoping it would be better, but in reality, it turned out to be worse." "Our situation here, so close to the yellow line, is tragic," Al-Basyouni continued. "We can't hide from the Israelis, and we can't hide from the militias." While Israeli forces have taken to shooting, shelling, and bombing Palestinians from afar on a regular basis, the Palestinian militias are deployed to raid areas on the ground. "The militias are constantly around here, and we're afraid of them. Suddenly, you find them surrounding the area with quadcopters, opening fire at us, and storming inside," Arafat Ali, who was displaced to the Jabaliya Services Club, told Drop Site. "Day and night, you find them coming in and attacking us. They recently beat four young men and detained one of them before leaving," he said, referring to the raid on Al-Sheikh's house. "Even the man they detained had nothing to do with any organization." "We don't even understand how they operate. Suddenly, they open fire at us, fire shells, take young men captive, and then leave," Ali continued. "They don't come during the day. They come at three in the morning, like bandits." There is no reliable count of how many people have been detained by Palestinian militias. Like many others, Said Okasha, Al-Sheikh's brother-in-law who was detained in the raid last month, is most likely imprisoned in one of Israel's detention camps where torture and abuse is systemic. Meanwhile, Al-Sheikh himself has struggled to come to terms with the violence of the raid. "It was truly horrific--more horrific than you can imagine. Even now, speaking personally, apart from what this has done to my wife and children, what happened to me has left me hysterical and hallucinating. I walk down the street and tears start falling on their own," he said. "No matter how much I describe the scene, I can't truly convey what it was like." March of the Yellow Line The yellow line that Israeli troops initially withdrew to as part of the ceasefire agreement in October 2025 gave them control of 53% of the eastern side of the Gaza Strip, as outlined on Israel's own military maps. In some places, the line is demarcated by yellow concrete blocks, but in most of Gaza the boundary is invisible. Since then, Israeli forces have steadily pushed in, driving Palestinians further west, and expanding their control to close to 70% of the enclave. Last week, Israeli troops moved further into Shujaiya, once a vast, densely populated neighborhood in eastern Gaza City. On October 11, displaced Palestinians who sought shelter in the area woke up to shooting and shelling by Israeli forces as they moved the yellow blocks some 200 meters further inward, sparking panic and another round of displacement. "The yellow line used to be approximately 200 meters away from us. This morning, it was only 10 meters away," Osama Mushtaha, 50, told Drop Site. Families in Shujaiya in eastern Gaza City are forced to flee following an attack by Israeli forces as they moved yellow blocks into the area, further expanding Israel's line of control. October 11, 2026. Video by Mohamed Ahmed. Throughout the day, exhausted families gathered their scant belongings, piling mattresses and bags on the dusty streets, forced to flee once again in a desperate search for shelter. "We're dying here every day because of the yellow line," Anis Herzallah, 30, said. "At night we have shelling, quadcopters, tanks, Apaches and F-16s--all of them attacking us from the yellow line. We can't live here anymore. " The blocks in Shujaiya now lie close to Salah Al-Din street, a historic thoroughfare running north to south along the length of the Gaza Strip. Every encroachment of the yellow line brings Israel troops and the collaborating Palestinian militias ever closer. "People are leaving, not knowing where they're supposed to go," a passerby said. "An Israeli tank and bulldozer advanced towards the area. They also have militias with them." Sara Al-Ramlawi, 33, has been displaced with her family repeatedly over the past three years, moving from one place to another every few months before arriving at Shujaiya several months ago, only to be driven away yet again. "We were forced out because they moved the yellow line closer, we have suffered so much," she told Drop Site. "We're heading into the unknown. This is our situation, and the situation of every family from Shujaiya living here." "We're not asking for a house. Just a piece of land where we can put up tents." name: Chad Bianco
subject: I Will Never Give Up on California
body:
Our fight is far from over. And I need you by my side.

| | | | | |
---
| |

Friends,
**The fight for California continues.**
Every day, I think about the state of distress California is in. Our once-beautiful state, once known for low crime, families moving in, and patriotism, has taken a wrong turn.

I have come to tell you that California's future is not inevitable. **California will be what you make of it** —what we make of it, together—and it can once again have very beautiful times.
**I speak to all of California** , not just Riverside, because every day I am fighting the corrupt Sacramento elite and standing up for your rights, which are being taken away. I have seen it firsthand.
---

**Click above — important message**

**Sacramento doesn’t want you to own a legal firearm.** They don’t want fair elections or lawful investigations into where there may be fraud. They give sanctuary to criminals, including criminal migrants and refuse to fund Prop 36, which voters in every California county supported. And the list goes on
**My re-election campaign for sheriff won’t be an easy battle.** The Democrats will do everything in their power to ensure we lose. That is why I humbly ask for your support. Now more than ever, in these difficult times, California needs a strong voice for law and order—one that stands up for the people when Sacramento refuses to listen.
I am asking each and every one of you to **contribute just $5** today to my re-election campaign as Riverside County Sheriff. If you could **make it a recurring contribution** , it would make all the difference in this fight.
**I will never give up on this state.** I ask you to join me.
Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County

Hi Peter – it's Senator Adam Schiff. I’m reaching out today on behalf of my friend and colleague George Whitesides. He’s one of the few Democrats who flipped a GOP-held seat in 2024, and he’s been doing a great job representing the San Fernando, Antelope, and Santa Clarita Valleys ever since. # [Musk to gift EVERY US kid a SpaceX share next year](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Elon Musk said he will give **[one of his SpaceX shares](https://substack.com/redirect/42b6fc88-6a65-4ad9-ba8e-038a2cf6ec9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** **[to every American child next year,](https://substack.com/redirect/42b6fc88-6a65-4ad9-ba8e-038a2cf6ec9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** calling it the first of many such gifts after urging Anthropic to distribute shares directly to the public rather than through a fund.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Direct public response:** Musk posted the pledge on X early Monday after telling Anthropic to give shares to people instead of routing them through a public-benefit entity.
* **Anthropic equity contrast:** The AI firm committed 5% of shares to its public benefit fund, with escalators that could reach about 20%, while co-founders pledged 80% of their equity.
* **Earnings calendar surprise:** SpaceX set an Oct. 20 after-market earnings date, weeks ahead of typical notice, as it seeks financing for Nvidia AI chips.
* **Financing structure:** The package includes about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt, with Apollo expected to help lead and PIMCO among potential participants.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..1rgJz8_u01YdPGSonhOHJy5CJkwWq-E16U88PmH4VFo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221159715)
* * *
* * *
# [Microsoft walks away from Nscale UK deal as neocloud stress widens](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
AI infrastructure stress spread further as **[Microsoft withdrew from an Nscale UK data-center site](https://substack.com/redirect/a8f88023-d06d-4732-bd7b-b9cdc2943f9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and investors roughly halved a $30 billion IPO valuation ask, while Morgan Stanley's AI basket logged its worst week ever.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Microsoft exit:** The hyperscaler walked away from the Loughton project amid multi-year power delays that push grid connection into the 2030s.
* **Valuation cut:** IPO investors slashed the roughly $30 billion ask roughly in half, echoing an earlier pulled listing by Firmus.
* **Basket collapse:** Morgan Stanley's AI Tech Beneficiaries basket fell 16.5%, its worst week since inception, while the S&P declined only about 2%.
* **Capex concentration:** Morgan Stanley mapping shows nearly $700 billion of 2027 AI capital spending landing at Nvidia versus roughly $340 billion for the other 499 S&P names.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..1rgJz8_u01YdPGSonhOHJy5CJkwWq-E16U88PmH4VFo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221159715)
* * *
# [Brent slips from near $110 as Hormuz risks and freight costs mount](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Brent crude eased to $108.52 on Monday **[after touching nearly $110 overnight,](https://substack.com/redirect/f0f80b7a-e61e-4341-b60b-144e694126d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as profit-taking met fresh tanker strikes and record Gulf-to-China freight rates that push landed costs toward $140 a barrel.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Hormuz flow hit:** Seven-day average Gulf crude flows fell to 8.5 million barrels a day last week from more than 20 million, with at least 10 vessel incidents.
* **Wright peak claim:** Energy Secretary Chris Wright said U.S. pump prices have peaked, with Gulf flows recovering to about 80% of pre-conflict levels.
* **Shipping squeeze:** Freight from the Gulf to China reached $33 a barrel by late September, forcing producers into deeper discounts to secure buyers.
* **Mine incident:** An Iranian-reported tanker fire and explosion after hitting a naval mine in the southern Strait added to the risk premium.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..1rgJz8_u01YdPGSonhOHJy5CJkwWq-E16U88PmH4VFo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221159715)
* * *
# [Trump DOE puts $42M behind stalled Constitution Pipeline](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Energy Department **[said it will put up to $42 million](https://substack.com/redirect/2a623d4a-44c5-4ce6-b3ed-5c351e1640e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Defense Production Act funds toward reviving the stalled Constitution Pipeline from Pennsylvania to New York.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Funding details:** The Title III money supports permitting and pre-construction work on the 125-mile line that would move up to 650,000,000,000 BTUs a day from the Marcellus Shale.
* **Timeline target:** Williams hopes construction begins next spring, with service by the fourth quarter of 2028 or the winter of 2028.
* **Wright supply push:** Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the answer to high prices is more supply and that the Northeast needs more energy for heating and generation.
* **Long stalled project:** Proposed in 2012 and federally approved in 2014, the line was abandoned in 2020 after New York denied a water-quality certificate and years of disputes.

* * *
# [Goldman gets picky over Bond ratings as AI debt floods credit](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs **[now favors BBB-rated bonds over higher-rated AAs](https://substack.com/redirect/d94aa644-bc5f-4ff0-8041-b194e44d667e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as artificial-intelligence-linked issuance floods investment-grade credit, while the cost of insuring Oracle against default has climbed sharply.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Rating preference shift:** The bank flagged balance-sheet deterioration at the top of the rating spectrum and potential for another roughly $22 billion of fallen angels in coming weeks.
* **Oracle stress test:** Five-year credit-default swaps on Oracle stood at 295 basis points after touching 300, up 287% in a year and trading more like high-yield levels.
* **Debt load:** Oracle has $118 billion in long-term debt plus $39 billion in capital and lease obligations, with free cash flow expected deeply negative through 2027.
* **Downgrade risk:** S&P rates the company BBB-, the lowest investment-grade tier, after a July cut; further pressure could force sales by grade-only investors.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..1rgJz8_u01YdPGSonhOHJy5CJkwWq-E16U88PmH4VFo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221159715)
* * *
# [JPMorgan puts $5 billion into national-security critical companies](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
JPMorgan Chase said it **[has invested $5 billion in equity in industries critical to U.S. economic and national security,](https://substack.com/redirect/a7082850-225d-4bfa-af3d-356dca3063a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while financing $230 billion in the first year of its security and resiliency initiative.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Equity deployment:** The $5 billion supports advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, and supply-chain resilience within a broader $1.5 trillion decade-long commitment.
* **Financed volume:** The bank arranged and facilitated more than $230 billion in transactions across supply chains, defense, energy, and advanced manufacturing.
* **Focus areas:** Investments target next-generation defense technologies, automated factories, distributed battery storage, and frontier technologies.
* **Advisor departure:** Separately, two teams overseeing $18.6 billion left to form independent Latigo Peak Partners.

# [China's economy expanded 4.5% in third quarter on exports](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
China's economy **[expanded 4.5% in the third quarter,](https://substack.com/redirect/e56059a8-07bc-401c-a916-b3a20320ecb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/e56059a8-07bc-401c-a916-b3a20320ecb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)powered by exports, while weak consumer confidence and the property slump still weigh.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f02ac31f-5f4e-470b-967f-ebc30b35c028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Growth rebound:** The 4.5% year-over-year print rose from 4.3% in the second quarter, the slowest pace since 2022.
* **Export offset:** Booming shipments, particularly in technology and AI-related goods, mitigated a deepening domestic slowdown.
* **Domestic drag:** Consumer confidence remains soft and the property market continues to weigh on activity.
* **Target track:** Growth of 4.6% over the first nine months leaves the economy on course for the official 4.5% to 5% annual goal.

body:
| | | |
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

body:
This race just shifted in our direction.
Folks, we just got incredible news, and I wanted you to see it right away.
**First:** We’ve been leading in the latest polls by as much as TWO points thanks to the support of this grassroots team funding our ads and helping us reach folks across Kansas.
**Then:** The Senate Leadership Fund – a major GOP super PAC – announced they’re funnelling $15 million to win this race by attacking me and propping up Roger Marshall.
**Now:** The attacks are working, team. The latest New York Times/Siena poll shows this race is a dead heat – just as **Nate Silver shifted his forecast for the Kansas Senate seat to a TOSS-UP.**
**[This shift is a true testament to everything this grassroots team has put into this campaign. Please, at this critical moment, will you chip in a split donation to my campaign and Aaron Ford as much as you can to help me keep up this momentum, hold the lead and flip this seat?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261019_3_ak.O7vzMd&amount=5&refcode=em20261019-1123&t=2&akid=1130%2E127862%2EVXkZSp)**

To celebrate the incredible progress we've made to get our ad on air, I went out hunting this past weekend!

Fall in the Northwoods is my favorite time of year. The air turns cold, the woods come alive, and it's a perfect time to be outdoors, whatever your interests. The changing seasons are part of a way of life.

That's also why I’m running. I meet a lot of people who work hard, love this region, and feel like Washington stopped working for them. They’re paying more for gas, groceries, and prescriptions, and Congress hasn’t done much to help.

I want to make the case that we can do so much better before November 3.

[**Plenty of voters in northern Wisconsin still get their news from local TV, and many haven’t heard from this campaign yet. name: Chris Pappas
subject: A literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9630%2E582294%2ES-5tYU ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9630%2E582294%2ES-5tYU ]Chris Pappas for Senate

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261019_2.9jNJpl&refcode=em20261019-9630&amount=5&t=1003&akid=9630%2E582294%2ES-5tYU ][IMG]
Josh Rogers/NHPR

At the GOP debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running
for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant."

He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who
cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the
heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.

I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.

My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour
week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up
every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter —
because they do.

John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life. He was born into
the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant
serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China.

That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”

New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor
actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant
workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is
running to protect people like himself. I'm running for everyone else.

He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he
doesn’t represent us.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261019_2.9jNJpl&amount=5&refcode=em20261019-2&t=1022&akid=9630%2E582294%2ES-5tYU ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. He doesn’t get how hard
we work — and he sure as hell doesn’t think our labor is worth respecting.

I do. That’s why I’m running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261019_2.9jNJpl&refcode=em20261019-9630&amount=5&t=1023&akid=9630%2E582294%2ES-5tYU ]Chris Pappas

name: Andrea Salinas
subject: We can do more to prevent future tragedies – and we must.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Andrea Salinas for Oregon
body:
https://www.andreasalinasfororegon.com/ [https://www.andreasalinasfororegon.com/] On Thursday afternoon, three children — ages 5, 8, and 11 — and a devoted teacher were killed in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary. I am heartbroken for their families, classmates, colleagues, and the entire Bend community.

And I am furious that, yet again, American families are burying their children and loved ones due to a horrifying act of gun violence.

Our nation’s never-ending cycle of mass shootings isn’t just tragic. It’s preventable. And it’s shameful that Washington won’t act when there is so much more we could do to stop this senseless loss of life.

I refuse to accept this kind of violence as normal U.S. culture. I refuse to accept as normal that students, teachers, and staff should ever fear for their lives at what should be a safe place for learning. I refuse to accept children and teachers being gunned down in their classroom as the unavoidable cost of freedom.

Congress can act, and we must.

Thank you,

Andrea Salinas

body:
I wrote this note with you in mind.

★★★★★

[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

Friend,

I clawed my way into this fight, fighting twice as hard, earning every
inch, and taking nothing for granted. I’m not backing down now.

I wrote this note with you in mind, because everything I’ve done,
every battle I’ve taken on, has only been possible because of
supporters like you.

They told me I couldn’t do it.
Said I was too young. Too conservative. Too outspoken.

They wanted me to stay in my lane. Sit still. Smile pretty.
_WELL, BLESS THEIR HEARTS. THEY HAD NO IDEA WHO THEY WERE DEALING
WITH, FRIEND._

I rolled up my sleeves, fought like hell, and shattered a glass
ceiling as the first woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate from
Alabama. I don’t just show up. I dig in, do the work, and refuse to
be outworked or outmatched.

Not because it was easy, but because this country is worth every ounce
of the fight.

I didn’t grow up dreaming of power. I grew up in Enterprise,
Alabama, where I learned the value of faith, family, and hard work.
I’m a Christian, a wife, a mom, and a proud conservative. _And I ran
for office because I couldn’t sit back while the Left tore apart
EVERYTHING we love._

Now? I’m doing exactly what I promised:

★
Calling out their lies.
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

★
Fighting back against their radical agenda.
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

★
Defending our values with everything I’ve got.
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

But make no mistake, the Left is pouring MILLIONS into flipping
conservative seats. And trust me, _THEY’RE FURIOUS MINE ISN’T UP
FOR GRABS._

So now? They’re setting their sights on every one of my conservative
friends and doing everything they can to crush our momentum, shut us
up, and take down anyone who dares to stand in their way.

They want us gone. Quiet. Out of the way.
_TOO BAD. I DIDN’T COME HERE TO MAKE FRIENDS. I CAME HERE TO CLEAN
HOUSE._

If you believe in what I’m fighting for, if you still believe this
country is worth saving, then I need you with me. THIS IS A GRASSROOTS
FIGHT, AND IT ONLY WORKS WHEN PEOPLE LIKE YOU CHIP IN. $5, $10,
WHATEVER YOU CAN GIVE HELPS US HOLD THE LINE AND KEEP FIGHTING LIKE
HELL:
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

★ CHIP IN ANY AMOUNT >>
[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

Because this isn’t just about me. This is about whether the America
we love survives, or gets ripped apart by people who mock our values,
trash our faith, and couldn’t care less what it means to work hard,
raise a family, or live with purpose.

I’m proud to have you standing with me.

- Katie Britt

[https://link.email.brittforsenate.

_U.S. Senator for Alabama_
_Christian. Conservative. Mom. Fighter._

WE’D BE SAD TO SEE YOU GO, BUT IF YOU WANT TO STOP RECEIVING OUR

Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. I almost missed the last flight to Lubbock a few days ago. We were stuck on the tarmac at DFW then sprinted through the airport to catch the connection. We made the plane, just barely.
It was worth it.
That night more than 400 people came out to our event. About half of them I’d met over the last eight years of visiting Lubbock. The other half are people I’d never seen before, because they just turned 18 and this is their first election.
The next day we organized on the Texas Tech campus, adding hundreds of new voters to our turnout program.
Lubbock has been written off by one party and taken for granted by the other.
This is exactly why Powered by People is organizing there. We show up where others don't and go to the places that are hard to get to.
If we win statewide this November for the first time in over 30 years, it’ll be because places like Lubbock came through.
