(You can watch my speech **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/d8397f96-b5f6-4f17-8687-898f1708b71e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**)
Here's what I said:
Now, over the last year, I've been in small towns and big cities. I've been in the mountains and on the coast and on the Georgia farms that feed and clothe the whole world.
Together, we've gathered in backyards and living rooms and at rallies like this one where the crowds just keep growing and growing. And after all that, I'm here to tell you that I have no doubt our victory is near at hand.
**In 17 days, Georgia, when the polls close, we 'll defeat the bigot congressman, Trump puppet Mike Collins. In 17 days, our juggernaut Democratic coordinated campaign will have turned out the vote like never before to elect Josh McLaurin, Penny Brown Reynolds, Tanya Miller, and Democrats up and down the ballot across our state. In 17 days, we'll elect Keisha Lance Bottoms the next governor of Georgia.**
Keisha is a mother of four, and as our governor, she'll guarantee pre-K for every four-year-old in Georgia. She'll expand Medicaid to save Georgia's hospitals and nursing homes and ensure every child in Georgia has great health care. It's time to elect Keisha Lance Bottoms our next governor and make sure no child in Georgia is turned away from the pediatrician.
And Georgia, in 17 days, we'll rebuke the crook President Donald J. Trump with such clarity and power that no president will dare such abuses again for centuries. But between now and then, we need you to work -- not for my sake, but for the sake of our state and our country.
See, some people just happen to live at times and in places where history is made. And this year, once again Georgia, that's us. So, Georgia, are you ready to work?
Now, maybe you saw Donald Trump was in Dalton yesterday... oblivious to the collapse of his presidency. A crowd smaller than this one endured two hours of senile babbling, while the price of oil hit its five month high.
Now remember, they promised to lower prices on day one. Instead, under the failed President Donald J. Trump, it costs more than ever in American history to fill up your truck, stock your fridge, visit the doctor, or power your home.
They promised to drain the swamp. Instead, it's the most corrupt administration of all time, and everybody knows it. Everybody knows it. And while the crook president and his crook family rake in billions from all over the world, you pay more for everything.
They doubled your insurance premiums and slashed Medicaid to cut taxes for the rich. They lied us into war and spent most of the last year covering up for the world's most famous pedophile.
At a rally earlier this week in Ohio, the president egged on supporters who assaulted a woman demanding the release of the Epstein files. Did you see that? Because if you can count on one thing about this White House, it's their tireless commitments to war, inflation, and covering up sex trafficking.
Now remember, they also promised peace. Instead, they plunged us into a war they don't know how to end or how to win. The biggest foreign policy debacle since Iraq and another war based on lies. Remember, last year they claimed Iran's nuclear program had been obliterated. Do you remember that? And then this year, they claimed that same nuclear program posed an imminent threat -- both times lying.
And now remember, on day four of the war, the president declared victory.
On day 11, Trump said, "The war is very complete." That was day 11.
Day 13, "We won."
Day 21, "Getting very close."
Day 32, "Leaving very soon."
On day 40, the president declared "Total and complete victory."
Today is day 232.
And yesterday in Dalton, he promised again the war would be over soon. He claimed again Iran's military had been destroyed. And he said he would rename Hormuz the Trump Strait.
See, the draft-dodging president tells jokes while 21 Americans are dead and hundreds wounded. Iran still has its uranium and its drones and its missiles. Diesel's at its all-time high. 12 more ships were hit this week alone. They've drained our stockpiles to achieve nothing, while the crook Commander in Chief builds a monument to himself.
And while the world burns, in Washington and at Mar-a-Lago it's a spectacle of graft unprecedented in American history.
Now maybe you saw Trump's so desperate he's begging Putin for diesel. But listen to this: At the very same time, the White House is brokering the sale of billions in Russian energy assets to people who fund the Trump family and the Trump campaign. We're talking oil fields, refineries, gas stations all over the world to be sold to the first family's cronies in a deal brokered and backed by the U.S. government.
Y'all remember Jared Kushner? The president's son-in-law, the so-called special envoy, responsible for diplomacy with Russia and in the Middle East. Do you remember the other special envoy, Steve Witkoff, who co-founded the president's crooked crypto business, World Liberty?
Okay, so follow me through on this -- what Jared and Steve are doing right now is negotiating with Putin to sell billions in Russian oil fields and refineries and gas stations to the president's friends.
You've got Sheikh Tahnoon, the Emirati spy chief who paid half a billion to the Trump-Witkoff crypto business. Then you've got the Al-Khayyat brothers, two Syrians who are financing Jared and Ivanka's multibillion dollar Albanian resort project. And then the third partner, a billionaire mega-donor to Trump's campaign.
Oh, and the U.S. government would take a 15% stake, by the way. Are you getting the picture? Amidst a global energy crisis, the president's son-in-law and the president's business partner are brokering the sale of Russian oil fields to the first family's friends. The same friends who have poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Trump family businesses.
And then there's Marco Rubio committing $1.6 billion of your money to back the Trump boys' mining interests in Kazakhstan. Did you hear about that? Pete Hegseth steering hundreds of millions of Pentagon dollars to back Don Jr.'s magnet investment. Venezuelan oil money turning up in Qatari bank accounts. Because, see, they are literally the elites they pretend to hate.
**And here 's the bottom line: If you're involved in any of this, next year you'll be raising your right hand and swearing to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, so help you God, in front of the United States Congress.**
The Mar-a-Lago mafia really has taken American corruption to spectacular new heights. But Georgia, corruption in American politics runs a lot deeper than Donald Trump. And see, I get why people voted for him.
_Because even before he came on the scene, American politics was coin-operated. Money goes in, favors come out. It 's been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money. Both sides. And when members of Congress aren't fundraising from lobbyists and corporate PACs, they're trying to dodge getting bombed by these Super PACs._
Spectacular wealth buys an ever greater share of power over our national affairs. And this corruption is why nothing works for ordinary people. It's why you pay a fortune for prescriptions. It's why your insurance company gets away with denying your cancer treatment after you paid your premiums for decades.
**So Trump promised to attack a broken system. I get it, ripe target. Yes, the system really is rigged, but he 's not unrigging it. He is re-rigging it for himself.**
And how do we unrig American politics? Well, first, follow the money. _Citizens United_ was the most destructive Supreme Court decision in modern American history. And Donald Trump's rise is a symptom. See, the crisis we must meet is deeper than this presidency.
Trump's rise is proof that business as usual has failed, that our politics, sickened by corruption, is failing the American public and compromising our national integrity, and that the hour is late to fix what's broken.
And I suspect many of you are here because you recognize that our task is not just to contain this wickedness, but to repair the brokenness beneath it. That this moment is an opening, not for restoration, but for reformation. Because who really supports allowing unlimited, secret political money to bend the nation's agenda in darkness?
In Athens or Albany or Columbus or College Park, if I ask anyone -- Democrat, independent, Republican, none of the above -- if I ask them whether this is how things should work, it doesn't matter who they are, the answer is no. So let the defenders of secret corporate money in politics come out and defend it. They'll lose the debate. And Georgia, if it takes a constitutional amendment to end _Citizens United_ , we'll deliver a United Georgia to ratify it.
_**A United Georgia.**_
Every day our wave grows taller and our tent grows bigger. Because this isn't just a campaign for Democrats. Folks come up to me at airports or on the street. They tell me they're lifelong Republicans, but this year, they're voting for Democrats for the first time.
Down in Valdosta, the mayor's named Scott James Matheson, a lifelong conservative Republican. We expanded Valdosta's transit system together. We upgraded Moody Air Force Base together. When Hurricane Helene hit, I called him up in the middle of the night to check on the city, and when the storm cleared, I was there alongside him to help, going block by block. We served hot meals to folks who had just lost their homes.
When I got back to Washington, I delivered federal disaster relief for South Georgia, and now I'm honored to have conservative Republican Mayor Matheson's support in this reelection campaign.
See, just about every week, I dial up Georgia mayors and pastors and farmers to find out how I can help. One day, I called up Mayor Julie Smith, just up the road from Valdosta in Tifton. Mayor Smith's a Republican, too. She told me the Tifton hospital needed new dialysis equipment. She explained how Tifton's dialysis center serves 12 South Georgia counties, and they just couldn't meet the need.
So I delivered the funds to upgrade that South Georgia clinic, and now it can serve 200 dialysis patients. And Republican Mayor Julie Smith is backing this campaign too.
Up north in Toccoa, then-Mayor Gail Fry, another Georgia Republican, she told me Toccoa's gas lines were wearing out, and a leak could risk lives. We needed to get moving quick to replace miles of old pipes. So I delivered the funds for Toccoa's new gas lines, and Georgia Republican Gail Fry's backing this campaign too.
Because, see, hurricanes and diabetes and gas leaks don't check your party affiliation when they hit. And when it comes to serving Georgia, I don't either.
But there's another reason so many Republicans are backing our campaign, and it's the bigot Congressman Mike Collins, who's only a congressman because his daddy was a congressman, surrounded at work, at home, and on his campaign by neo-Nazis and white nationalists.
See, Brian Kemp was right about Mike. There's a reason Rick Jackson doesn't campaign with Mike. Why Brad Raffensperger refuses to endorse him. Why conservative WSB radio host Shelley Wynter called Mike a bottom feeder.
Why Coach Dooley condemned Mike's "blatant taxpayer-funded corruption," and said Mike's "disgusting behavior does not represent Georgia values or, frankly, any values."
Why Erick Erickson said Mike "knowingly hired a sociopath with a criminal record who was alleged to have used your and my tax dollars to subsidize his girlfriend."
There's a reason one of the founders of the Tea Party said this summer "I cannot in conscience vote for Mike Collins. He is unfit for office," and warned that Collins would "drag down the whole Republican ticket in Georgia."
And that reason is that Mike Collins is a known bigot under federal investigation for the illegal misuse of tax dollars, widely known for his poor character and low integrity, and unfit for any elected office in the United States. And Georgia, now the bigot wants a promotion. But this year, we'll end his political career instead.
Because in his pathetic, childlike devotion to Donald Trump, Mike Collins has sold out our state. He voted every time for the war. He voted every time for the tariffs. He voted to double your health insurance premiums and for the biggest Medicaid cut in American history.
Listen to this: St. Mary's Hospital in Lavonia is in Mike's district. And they just closed their maternity unit, citing the Medicaid cuts that Mike Collins voted for to fund tax cuts for the rich.
So now, thanks to Mike Collins, delivering mothers Mike Collins represents have to drive an hour in labor to get to a labor and delivery unit, in a state where we've already lost 21 hospitals in 20 years.
In a state where if you're born today in Georgia, your life expectancy is shorter than if you were born today in Lebanon. Where, thanks to Donald Trump and Mike Collins, and their attacks on the Affordable Care Act, 300,000 Georgians lost their health insurance this year, and a million saw their premiums double.
Now what could drive a man, even one as spoiled and hateful as the congressman's son Mike Collins, to cast votes that close a labor and delivery unit in his own district? Or double his own constituents' health insurance premiums? See, it's not just the money that's corrupted our politics, it's moral corruption. The cynical indifference of powerful people.
See, my office is known for world-class service. But what amazes me is how surprised people are to be treated well.
Nancy Lancy's 81 years old in Jesup. Her husband died after years of dementia. She was worn out and alone. And now her affairs as a widow were all wrapped up in this bureaucratic labyrinth from the VA to the IRS and Social Security. So we took care of things for her.
**And I 'll never forget what she said about it. She said, "This was a new experience, to have someone caring about me." A new experience to have someone caring about me.**
How has it come to pass that for so many Americans, the experience of genuine care is rare and surprising? Official indifference and corporate disrespect have become systemic when millions are just one medical bill, one short paycheck, one bad alternator from financial disaster.
You work harder and harder, but the treadmill gets faster and steeper and the bills get higher and higher. A 60-hour workweek still needs SNAP, and that bucket list trip's off the table for good.
And then, instead of reading your daughter her favorite book, that precious spare hour after work you're on the phone begging the insurance company to cover the medicine that prevents her seizures.
The Army lost the records you need to claim your VA benefits, and it takes a year and 12 phone calls to fix it. You report the black mold to your landlord, who doesn't fix the leak, and the ambulance for your toddler's asthma is followed by a $3,000 bill.
And it's the worst for the most vulnerable. Maybe you saw my investigation of Georgia foster care. In just four years, hundreds of Georgia children likely sex trafficked in the care of our state. Many more abused and neglected. Rachel Aldridge testified about her two-year-old daughter, Brooklynn. See, over Rachel's repeated objections, DFCS had placed two-year-old Brooklynn in the care of her father and his girlfriend, despite their criminal histories.
State officials ignored Rachel's pleas. They skipped mandatory background checks. And two months later, Rachel's precious, perfect, irreplaceable, two-year-old girl was dead. When she testified before my committee, Rachel said she had flown on an airplane for the first time in her life just so she could tell Senators her story. She begged us, "Please remember Brooklynn."
And listen to this, Georgia DFCS is so broken that when they couldn't find enough placements for kids with special needs, the DFCS commissioner tried to lock those kids up in jails for children. But the judges refused and reported it to my office.
_They tried to put special needs kids in jail._
And then when my investigation brought all this to light, when we held Senate hearings and exposed it all, instead of resigning or at least leaping into action to fix it, state officials retreated into denial and PR and counterattack.
Because foster kids don't have lobbyists or a Super PAC. Neither do the women subjected to medical abuse in ICE detention. Neither do the female inmates sexually abused by the warden and the chaplain in their federal prison. Or the young military family neglected by the defense contractor with a 50-year lease on privatized housing at Fort Gordon.
But they deserve leaders who see them and expose those who abuse them, and that's exactly what I'll keep doing, Georgia, because we're all in this together.
Every day, I think about Congressman Lewis. His portrait hangs right above my desk in my Senate office. And even in his final moments, he kept reminding us that we all live in one American house, that we all live in one world house. Do you remember? John Lewis called it the inevitable truth that we're all members of one human family.
And I suspect many of you are here today because you're so deeply troubled by the pain that so many of our fellow human beings are enduring right now -- the terror of a child watching ICE take away his mother, the despair of a cancer patient losing coverage mid-treatment, or the silent panic of a grandmother when she sees the receipt for her groceries and then remembers there's three weeks left until her next Social Security check.
And that ache in your heart, that pit in your stomach, that feeling's what reminds us that we're all in this together. That we're not just one United States, we're one united people. E pluribus unum. Out of many, one.
How inspiring that the most powerful nation on Earth proclaims as our core values that all are created equal, with inalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness? Because see, Americans aren't a race. We're a people. United not by ethnicity but by shared convictions, and that is what makes us exceptional and a beacon to the world.
**And see, this is what small men like Donald Trump and Mike Collins will never understand -- that our national greatness flows not through our blood or our genes but through our ideas, our aspirations, and our care for one another.**
Mike Collins, who put people with Klan ties in campaign leadership roles, who personally himself has promoted neo-Nazi propaganda, who praised a mob that was harassing a Black woman on a college campus with monkey sounds.
And I don't know if you saw the debates last week. _Mike, if you want to go again, I 'm ready. I'm ready, Mike._
See, at last week's debate, he couldn't even bring himself to say he'd stop the production of neo-Nazi propaganda from his own house. Did you see that? I told Mike we could shake on it. All he had to do was stop neo-Nazi propaganda from his house for three weeks. He refused.
Just stop and think about this for a second. A sitting Congressman currently running for the Senate hosts a neo-Nazi at his house, and that neo-Nazi produces neo-Nazi propaganda from his house, and the Congressman won't, or maybe can't, get the neo-Nazi in his house to stop producing neo-Nazi content from his house while he's running for the United States Senate.
A crumbling little bigot. See, Georgia, a man who won't take responsibility for what happens under his own roof can't be trusted with our national affairs. That's not the only question Mike won't answer. Mike's like a scandal piñata. Every time you shake him more misdeeds fall out.
He's not just surrounded by white nationalists, he's also under federal investigation for the illegal misuse of tax dollars. And rather than come clean, the Office of Congressional Conduct reports that Mike "refused to cooperate." They recommended he be subpoenaed and forced to testify. And Mike won't even say if he'll testify. Listen, Georgia, Mike Collins needs to testify.
**See, Georgia deserves so much better than this. And America deserves so much better than Donald Trump.** Just think, 250 years on, what the founders would see if they visited us today. They'd see that slavery had been abolished. They'd see that Americans without land and then women and then the descendants of slaves had secured voting rights.
They'd see that our science and technology propelled human knowledge to unimaginable heights and that those 13 colonies grew into a superpower that defeated the Nazis and communism. They'd see a pluralist democracy, people descended from every point on Earth of all colors stitched together out of many nations into one.
But they'd also see a nation that, at the height of its wealth and power, fell into the very traps they most feared. Consumed by bitter conflict between rival factions captured by special interests. Losing touch with that great national spirit that defeated fascism and landed men on the moon.
They'd see that we did those great things but then succumbed to a small and self-serving politics, unmoored from fixed moral principles, incapable of inspiration or great national achievement, with no real horizon beyond the next election.
And they'd see that what's required of us now is far, far greater than what that small, self-serving politics can muster.
I've got two little girls at home. Eva's four, and Lila's one. And I'm so grateful to this country for the security and opportunity it affords them. But this isn't the world I want to leave them. Soon enough, they'll learn there's now plastic in human blood and breast milk, that toxic forever chemicals are in half the country's drinking water.
Eva loves animal documentaries and she'll learn that the butterflies are dying off. She'll learn about the nuclear weapons that still threaten annihilation. She'll ask me why I allowed these things to happen. And when you step back and consider it, the situation's absurd.
Tech titans dig bunkers while warning us the artificial intelligence they're creating risks human extinction. Meanwhile, our Congress debates youth sports, and the president builds a ballroom. An ancient establishment barely capable of email sleepwalks into a technological revolution while the president dismantles precautions and calls us fools for worrying.
And what fills us with dread is the crushing weakness of our politics against the massive stakes of our times. You see this scenario, and you look at the state of our politics, and it shakes your faith in the future. I get it.
**But Georgia, we can and will reclaim control over our own destiny. We can and will meet our obligations to our children. And that begins with victory this fall, because Georgia, I refuse to leave my girls a world as dark and dangerous and cruel as this one threatens to become.**
And I can't stop thinking about it. I refuse to accept that Eva and Lila will grow up with artificial friends and teachers in a society where the sick die, not because there's no cure, but because they have no money.
Where we have enough nuclear weapons to destroy the world a thousandfold, but we still refuse to guarantee health care for every citizen. On a poisoned planet rearming for world war where human life is cheap and might makes right.
_See, when Eva 's old enough to ask me why I let this happen, I'm determined to answer truthfully that I didn't. I'll tell her how the same year she turned five, Georgia overcame every doubt and dirty trick, not just to win, but to set a new course for our state and our country and the world. I'll tell her our generation didn't shrink from its obligations to hers._
That instead we came together, clear-eyed about the stakes and what was required of us. That we protected the sanctity of the vote and defeated those who attacked it. That we elected those who understood the moment and had the will to meet it.
That we restored American leadership toward peace and human rights. That we guaranteed health care for every citizen, and that we mastered technology instead of letting it master us. That we ensured each generation achieves health and prosperity greater than the last. And that we lived up to the promise of equal justice for all.
**We can and will do these things, and it starts with victory in 17 days, Georgia.** Because, Georgia, our power's right there, just waiting for us to pick it up. Freedoms guaranteed at our founding, made real through struggle and sacrifice in places like Seneca Falls and Selma and Stonewall.
Over centuries, despite our sins and through courageous struggle, the flame of American freedom has grown brighter and bolder and given hope to the whole world. But we see that in the winds that blow today, that light is flickering.
The Fulton County ballot raid, executive orders attacking voting, the MAGA loyalists on our state Election Board. The election deniers and insurrectionists and their accomplices have made their plans very clear.
But when voting rights and civil rights that heroes marched and died to secure are under attack, we defend those rights by using them. And that's why Georgia Democrats are answering with a mobilization so massive and a defense of voting rights so fierce that no plot against the franchise will foil the will of the people.
Because how foolish of them to come to the cradle of the Civil Rights Movement to spread those lies and seize those ballots. They launched an attack on voting rights at the political and spiritual center of the very Black history they seek to erase.
And their attacks have only strengthened our resolve. And when we do what we must do, the sound of feet marching to the polls this fall will be heard in every corner of our state and all the way up on high, where Congressman John Lewis will look down and see a job well done.
See, Georgia, a wave is building -- the kind of wave that comes once a generation, when the people have been pushed too far, and they decide all together, all at once to say enough is enough.
We have 17 days, Georgia. The polls are open. Find yours at **[IWillVote.com](https://substack.com/redirect/adeb8755-2cb8-4951-8d74-ca1c2d5be077?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
Georgia, are you ready to vote? Are you ready to win? Thank you. God bless you. Let's get it done together. Thank you so much.

See, the draft-dodging president tells jokes while 21 Americans are dead and hundreds wounded. Iran still has its uranium and its drones and its missiles. We're talking oil fields, refineries, gas stations all over the world to be sold to the first family's cronies in a deal brokered and backed by the U.S. government. Y'all remember Jared Kushner? The president's son-in-law, the so-called special envoy, responsible for diplomacy with Russia and in the Middle East. Do you remember the other special envoy, Steve Witkoff, who co-founded the president's crooked crypto business, World Liberty? Okay, so follow me through on this -- what Jared and Steve are doing right now is negotiating with Putin to sell billions in Russian oil fields and refineries and gas stations to the president's friends. You've got Sheikh Tahnoon, the Emirati spy chief who paid half a billion to the Trump-Witkoff crypto business. Then you've got the Al-Khayyat brothers, two Syrians who are financing Jared and Ivanka's multibillion dollar Albanian resort project. And then the third partner, a billionaire mega-donor to Trump's campaign. Oh, and the U.S. government would take a 15% stake, by the way. Are you getting the picture? Amidst a global energy crisis, the president's son-in-law and the president's business partner are brokering the sale of Russian oil fields to the first family's friends. The same friends who have poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Trump family businesses. And then there's Marco Rubio committing $1.6 billion of your money to back the Trump boys' mining interests in Kazakhstan. Did you hear about that? Pete Hegseth steering hundreds of millions of Pentagon dollars to back Don Jr.'s magnet investment. Venezuelan oil money turning up in Qatari bank accounts. Because, see, they are literally the elites they pretend to hate. And here 's the bottom line: If you're involved in any of this, next year you'll be raising your right hand and swearing to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, so help you God, in front of the United States Congress. The Mar-a-Lago mafia really has taken American corruption to spectacular new heights. But Georgia, corruption in American politics runs a lot deeper than Donald Trump. And see, I get why people voted for him. Because even before he came on the scene, American politics was coin-operated. Money goes in, favors come out. It 's been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money. Both sides. And when members of Congress aren't fundraising from lobbyists and corporate PACs, they're trying to dodge getting bombed by these Super PACs. Spectacular wealth buys an ever greater share of power over our national affairs. And this corruption is why nothing works for ordinary people. It's why you pay a fortune for prescriptions. It's why your insurance company gets away with denying your cancer treatment after you paid your premiums for decades. So Trump promised to attack a broken system. I get it, ripe target. Yes, the system really is rigged, but he 's not unrigging it. He is re-rigging it for himself. And how do we unrig American politics? Well, first, follow the money. Citizens United was the most destructive Supreme Court decision in modern American history. And Donald Trump's rise is a symptom. See, the crisis we must meet is deeper than this presidency. Trump's rise is proof that business as usual has failed, that our politics, sickened by corruption, is failing the American public and compromising our national integrity, and that the hour is late to fix what's broken. And I suspect many of you are here because you recognize that our task is not just to contain this wickedness, but to repair the brokenness beneath it. That this moment is an opening, not for restoration, but for reformation. Because who really supports allowing unlimited, secret political money to bend the nation's agenda in darkness? In Athens or Albany or Columbus or College Park, if I ask anyone -- Democrat, independent, Republican, none of the above -- if I ask them whether this is how things should work, it doesn't matter who they are, the answer is no. So let the defenders of secret corporate money in politics come out and defend it. They'll lose the debate. And Georgia, if it takes a constitutional amendment to end Citizens United , we'll deliver a United Georgia to ratify it. A United Georgia. Every day our wave grows taller and our tent grows bigger. Because this isn't just a campaign for Democrats. Folks come up to me at airports or on the street. They tell me they're lifelong Republicans, but this year, they're voting for Democrats for the first time. Down in Valdosta, the mayor's named Scott James Matheson, a lifelong conservative Republican. We expanded Valdosta's transit system together. We upgraded Moody Air Force Base together. When Hurricane Helene hit, I called him up in the middle of the night to check on the city, and when the storm cleared, I was there alongside him to help, going block by block. We served hot meals to folks who had just lost their homes. When I got back to Washington, I delivered federal disaster relief for South Georgia, and now I'm honored to have conservative Republican Mayor Matheson's support in this reelection campaign. See, just about every week, I dial up Georgia mayors and pastors and farmers to find out how I can help. One day, I called up Mayor Julie Smith, just up the road from Valdosta in Tifton. Mayor Smith's a Republican, too. She told me the Tifton hospital needed new dialysis equipment. She explained how Tifton's dialysis center serves 12 South Georgia counties, and they just couldn't meet the need. So I delivered the funds to upgrade that South Georgia clinic, and now it can serve 200 dialysis patients. And Republican Mayor Julie Smith is backing this campaign too. Up north in Toccoa, then-Mayor Gail Fry, another Georgia Republican, she told me Toccoa's gas lines were wearing out, and a leak could risk lives. We needed to get moving quick to replace miles of old pipes. So I delivered the funds for Toccoa's new gas lines, and Georgia Republican Gail Fry's backing this campaign too. Because, see, hurricanes and diabetes and gas leaks don't check your party affiliation when they hit. And when it comes to serving Georgia, I don't either. But there's another reason so many Republicans are backing our campaign, and it's the bigot Congressman Mike Collins, who's only a congressman because his daddy was a congressman, surrounded at work, at home, and on his campaign by neo-Nazis and white nationalists. See, Brian Kemp was right about Mike. There's a reason Rick Jackson doesn't campaign with Mike. Why Brad Raffensperger refuses to endorse him. Why conservative WSB radio host Shelley Wynter called Mike a bottom feeder. Why Coach Dooley condemned Mike's "blatant taxpayer-funded corruption," and said Mike's "disgusting behavior does not represent Georgia values or, frankly, any values." Why Erick Erickson said Mike "knowingly hired a sociopath with a criminal record who was alleged to have used your and my tax dollars to subsidize his girlfriend." There's a reason one of the founders of the Tea Party said this summer "I cannot in conscience vote for Mike Collins. He is unfit for office," and warned that Collins would "drag down the whole Republican ticket in Georgia." And that reason is that Mike Collins is a known bigot under federal investigation for the illegal misuse of tax dollars, widely known for his poor character and low integrity, and unfit for any elected office in the United States. And Georgia, now the bigot wants a promotion. But this year, we'll end his political career instead. Because in his pathetic, childlike devotion to Donald Trump, Mike Collins has sold out our state. He voted every time for the war. He voted every time for the tariffs. He voted to double your health insurance premiums and for the biggest Medicaid cut in American history. Listen to this: St. Mary's Hospital in Lavonia is in Mike's district. And they just closed their maternity unit, citing the Medicaid cuts that Mike Collins voted for to fund tax cuts for the rich. So now, thanks to Mike Collins, delivering mothers Mike Collins represents have to drive an hour in labor to get to a labor and delivery unit, in a state where we've already lost 21 hospitals in 20 years. In a state where if you're born today in Georgia, your life expectancy is shorter than if you were born today in Lebanon. Where, thanks to Donald Trump and Mike Collins, and their attacks on the Affordable Care Act, 300,000 Georgians lost their health insurance this year, and a million saw their premiums double. Now what could drive a man, even one as spoiled and hateful as the congressman's son Mike Collins, to cast votes that close a labor and delivery unit in his own district? Or double his own constituents' health insurance premiums? See, it's not just the money that's corrupted our politics, it's moral corruption. The cynical indifference of powerful people. See, my office is known for world-class service. But what amazes me is how surprised people are to be treated well. Nancy Lancy's 81 years old in Jesup. Her husband died after years of dementia. She was worn out and alone. And now her affairs as a widow were all wrapped up in this bureaucratic labyrinth from the VA to the IRS and Social Security. So we took care of things for her. And I 'll never forget what she said about it. She said, "This was a new experience, to have someone caring about me." A new experience to have someone caring about me. How has it come to pass that for so many Americans, the experience of genuine care is rare and surprising? Official indifference and corporate disrespect have become systemic when millions are just one medical bill, one short paycheck, one bad alternator from financial disaster. You work harder and harder, but the treadmill gets faster and steeper and the bills get higher and higher. A 60-hour workweek still needs SNAP, and that bucket list trip's off the table for good. And then, instead of reading your daughter her favorite book, that precious spare hour after work you're on the phone begging the insurance company to cover the medicine that prevents her seizures. The Army lost the records you need to claim your VA benefits, and it takes a year and 12 phone calls to fix it. You report the black mold to your landlord, who doesn't fix the leak, and the ambulance for your toddler's asthma is followed by a $3,000 bill. And it's the worst for the most vulnerable. Maybe you saw my investigation of Georgia foster care. In just four years, hundreds of Georgia children likely sex trafficked in the care of our state. Many more abused and neglected. Rachel Aldridge testified about her two-year-old daughter, Brooklynn. See, over Rachel's repeated objections, DFCS had placed two-year-old Brooklynn in the care of her father and his girlfriend, despite their criminal histories. State officials ignored Rachel's pleas. They skipped mandatory background checks. And two months later, Rachel's precious, perfect, irreplaceable, two-year-old girl was dead. When she testified before my committee, Rachel said she had flown on an airplane for the first time in her life just so she could tell Senators her story. She begged us, "Please remember Brooklynn." And listen to this, Georgia DFCS is so broken that when they couldn't find enough placements for kids with special needs, the DFCS commissioner tried to lock those kids up in jails for children. But the judges refused and reported it to my office. They tried to put special needs kids in jail. And then when my investigation brought all this to light, when we held Senate hearings and exposed it all, instead of resigning or at least leaping into action to fix it, state officials retreated into denial and PR and counterattack. Because foster kids don't have lobbyists or a Super PAC. Neither do the women subjected to medical abuse in ICE detention. Neither do the female inmates sexually abused by the warden and the chaplain in their federal prison. Or the young military family neglected by the defense contractor with a 50-year lease on privatized housing at Fort Gordon. But they deserve leaders who see them and expose those who abuse them, and that's exactly what I'll keep doing, Georgia, because we're all in this together. Every day, I think about Congressman Lewis. His portrait hangs right above my desk in my Senate office. And even in his final moments, he kept reminding us that we all live in one American house, that we all live in one world house. Do you remember? John Lewis called it the inevitable truth that we're all members of one human family. And I suspect many of you are here today because you're so deeply troubled by the pain that so many of our fellow human beings are enduring right now -- the terror of a child watching ICE take away his mother, the despair of a cancer patient losing coverage mid-treatment, or the silent panic of a grandmother when she sees the receipt for her groceries and then remembers there's three weeks left until her next Social Security check. And that ache in your heart, that pit in your stomach, that feeling's what reminds us that we're all in this together. That we're not just one United States, we're one united people. E pluribus unum. Out of many, one. How inspiring that the most powerful nation on Earth proclaims as our core values that all are created equal, with inalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness? Because see, Americans aren't a race. We're a people. United not by ethnicity but by shared convictions, and that is what makes us exceptional and a beacon to the world. And see, this is what small men like Donald Trump and Mike Collins will never understand -- that our national greatness flows not through our blood or our genes but through our ideas, our aspirations, and our care for one another. Mike Collins, who put people with Klan ties in campaign leadership roles, who personally himself has promoted neo-Nazi propaganda, who praised a mob that was harassing a Black woman on a college campus with monkey sounds. And I don't know if you saw the debates last week. Mike, if you want to go again, I 'm ready. I'm ready, Mike. See, at last week's debate, he couldn't even bring himself to say he'd stop the production of neo-Nazi propaganda from his own house. Did you see that? I told Mike we could shake on it. All he had to do was stop neo-Nazi propaganda from his house for three weeks. He refused. Just stop and think about this for a second. A sitting Congressman currently running for the Senate hosts a neo-Nazi at his house, and that neo-Nazi produces neo-Nazi propaganda from his house, and the Congressman won't, or maybe can't, get the neo-Nazi in his house to stop producing neo-Nazi content from his house while he's running for the United States Senate. A crumbling little bigot. See, Georgia, a man who won't take responsibility for what happens under his own roof can't be trusted with our national affairs. That's not the only question Mike won't answer. Mike's like a scandal piñata. Every time you shake him more misdeeds fall out. He's not just surrounded by white nationalists, he's also under federal investigation for the illegal misuse of tax dollars. And rather than come clean, the Office of Congressional Conduct reports that Mike "refused to cooperate." They recommended he be subpoenaed and forced to testify. And Mike won't even say if he'll testify. Listen, Georgia, Mike Collins needs to testify. See, Georgia deserves so much better than this. And America deserves so much better than Donald Trump. Just think, 250 years on, what the founders would see if they visited us today. They'd see that slavery had been abolished. They'd see that Americans without land and then women and then the descendants of slaves had secured voting rights. They'd see that our science and technology propelled human knowledge to unimaginable heights and that those 13 colonies grew into a superpower that defeated the Nazis and communism. They'd see a pluralist democracy, people descended from every point on Earth of all colors stitched together out of many nations into one. But they'd also see a nation that, at the height of its wealth and power, fell into the very traps they most feared. Consumed by bitter conflict between rival factions captured by special interests. Losing touch with that great national spirit that defeated fascism and landed men on the moon. They'd see that we did those great things but then succumbed to a small and self-serving politics, unmoored from fixed moral principles, incapable of inspiration or great national achievement, with no real horizon beyond the next election. And they'd see that what's required of us now is far, far greater than what that small, self-serving politics can muster. I've got two little girls at home. Eva's four, and Lila's one. And I'm so grateful to this country for the security and opportunity it affords them. But this isn't the world I want to leave them. Soon enough, they'll learn there's now plastic in human blood and breast milk, that toxic forever chemicals are in half the country's drinking water. Eva loves animal documentaries and she'll learn that the butterflies are dying off. She'll learn about the nuclear weapons that still threaten annihilation. She'll ask me why I allowed these things to happen. And when you step back and consider it, the situation's absurd. Tech titans dig bunkers while warning us the artificial intelligence they're creating risks human extinction. Meanwhile, our Congress debates youth sports, and the president builds a ballroom. An ancient establishment barely capable of email sleepwalks into a technological revolution while the president dismantles precautions and calls us fools for worrying. And what fills us with dread is the crushing weakness of our politics against the massive stakes of our times. You see this scenario, and you look at the state of our politics, and it shakes your faith in the future. I get it. But Georgia, we can and will reclaim control over our own destiny. We can and will meet our obligations to our children. And that begins with victory this fall, because Georgia, I refuse to leave my girls a world as dark and dangerous and cruel as this one threatens to become. And I can't stop thinking about it. I refuse to accept that Eva and Lila will grow up with artificial friends and teachers in a society where the sick die, not because there's no cure, but because they have no money. Where we have enough nuclear weapons to destroy the world a thousandfold, but we still refuse to guarantee health care for every citizen. On a poisoned planet rearming for world war where human life is cheap and might makes right. See, when Eva 's old enough to ask me why I let this happen, I'm determined to answer truthfully that I didn't. I'll tell her how the same year she turned five, Georgia overcame every doubt and dirty trick, not just to win, but to set a new course for our state and our country and the world. I'll tell her our generation didn't shrink from its obligations to hers. That instead we came together, clear-eyed about the stakes and what was required of us. That we protected the sanctity of the vote and defeated those who attacked it. That we elected those who understood the moment and had the will to meet it. That we restored American leadership toward peace and human rights. That we guaranteed health care for every citizen, and that we mastered technology instead of letting it master us. That we ensured each generation achieves health and prosperity greater than the last. And that we lived up to the promise of equal justice for all. We can and will do these things, and it starts with victory in 17 days, Georgia. Because, Georgia, our power's right there, just waiting for us to pick it up. Freedoms guaranteed at our founding, made real through struggle and sacrifice in places like Seneca Falls and Selma and Stonewall. Over centuries, despite our sins and through courageous struggle, the flame of American freedom has grown brighter and bolder and given hope to the whole world. But we see that in the winds that blow today, that light is flickering. The Fulton County ballot raid, executive orders attacking voting, the MAGA loyalists on our state Election Board. The election deniers and insurrectionists and their accomplices have made their plans very clear. But when voting rights and civil rights that heroes marched and died to secure are under attack, we defend those rights by using them. And that's why Georgia Democrats are answering with a mobilization so massive and a defense of voting rights so fierce that no plot against the franchise will foil the will of the people. Because how foolish of them to come to the cradle of the Civil Rights Movement to spread those lies and seize those ballots. They launched an attack on voting rights at the political and spiritual center of the very Black history they seek to erase. And their attacks have only strengthened our resolve. And when we do what we must do, the sound of feet marching to the polls this fall will be heard in every corner of our state and all the way up on high, where Congressman John Lewis will look down and see a job well done. See, Georgia, a wave is building -- the kind of wave that comes once a generation, when the people have been pushed too far, and they decide all together, all at once to say enough is enough. We have 17 days, Georgia. The polls are open. Find yours at . Georgia, are you ready to vote? Are you ready to win? Thank you. God bless you. Let's get it done together. Thank you so much. 👋 Wait! Before you go... 👋 Jon Ossoff in Georgia is the ONLY Democratic Senator running for reelection in a state Trump won. He is MAGA's #1 target in the 2026 midterms. ** | | | | | (C) 2026 Jon Ossoff P.O. body:
Not everyone is paying attention to state-level races. You’re different, Peter

---
Peter, it’s Barack. More people should be paying attention to the key state-level elections on the ballot this November. Because with so much at stake, _it's hard to overstate the importance of these races to the future of our country_. That’s because leaders at the state level oversee elections. They draw the maps for Congress and state legislatures. They make decisions that ultimately make it easier (or harder) to vote. And with free and fair elections under attack — from mid-decade gerrymandering and threats of voter suppression — we need more state-level officials who care about building a stronger democracy. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee, which I co-founded with Attorney General Eric Holder, fights alongside its affiliates to elect state lawmakers and governors who are on the side of the people — who believe in fair maps and fair access to the ballot. The NDRC also fights to elect fair-minded judges who won’t bend the law or twist the rules of our democracy to help out a political party. **[The NDRC needs your help. They’ve endorsed over 300 Democracy Defenders who are up for election in 19 days in over a dozen states across the country. And they need more grassroots donations to help get leaders like them over the finish line so they can fight for fair maps across the country. More people should be paying attention to the key state-level elections on the ballot this November. Because with so much at stake, it's hard to overstate the importance of these races to the future of our country. That’s because leaders at the state level oversee elections. They draw the maps for Congress and state legislatures. They make decisions that ultimately make it easier (or harder) to vote. And with free and fair elections under attack — from mid-decade gerrymandering and threats of voter suppression — we need more state-level officials who care about building a stronger democracy. "Whoever acknowledges me before others, I will also acknowledge before my Father in heaven" Matthew 10:32
On a February morning in 2015, on a beach near Sirte, Libya, twenty-one men knelt in orange jumpsuits along the waterline. Behind each one stood a masked executioner. ISIS filmed the massacre and released it under a title that still chills: A Message Signed with Blood to the Nation of the Cross.
Twenty of the men were Coptic Christians from poor villages in Minya, Egypt -- day laborers who had migrated to Libya for the oldest reason men migrate: to send money home to people they loved. The twenty-first was different. His name, as best the world could recover it, was Matthew Ayariga, and he was from Ghana. He was not Coptic. By most accounts he was not a committed Christian at all when the militants sorted their captives -- Muslims to one side, Christians to the other -- and he ended up kneeling with the believers.

body:
Peter, Early Voting Has Begun. Nevada Needs YOU!

| | | | | | |
#### [DrewForNevada.com](https://us.list-manage.com/wgDQZPugbQG?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [](https://us.list-manage.com/10ax3JlDL2j?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)

---](https://us.list-manage.com/1D53uReU_lk?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| | | | | |
Peter -Early voting is officially underway in Nevada, and I have one message for you: **We cannot afford to sit this election out. **Between now and Election Day on November 3, Nevadans will make decisions that will shape the future of our state for years to come. Every statewide constitutional office is on the ballot. Our congressional races are critically important. And Democrats are fighting to gain supermajorities in both the Nevada State Senate and Assembly.**THE STAKES COULDN’T BE ANY HIGHER.**
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/nooyeg0yg3Z?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| | | | | | | | | | | |
And here's what I really want you to understand: **These races are CLOSE. **
We've seen Nevada elections decided by razor-thin margins. **Some races are won or lost by less than 1% of the vote.** That means your vote—and the votes of your friends, family, coworkers, and neighbors—could literally be the difference between winning and losing.
So I'm asking you to do more than just cast your ballot.
**SHOW UP. BRING SOMEONE WITH YOU. SPREAD THE WORD.**
Talk to your neighbors. Remind your coworkers. Call a friend who doesn't always vote in midterm elections. Make sure the people around you understand just how much is on the line.
**And that every single vote counts.**
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1B09fJbT5W7?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/5TIhNzwSTF4?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| |

## The Energy Across Nevada is Incredible!
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
I had the opportunity to kick off early voting this weekend alongside **Governor Joe Lombardo,** campaigning across Northern Nevada with stops in Carson City, Reno, and Douglas County.
One of the highlights was speaking at the**Douglas County Republican Party's Heritage BBQ in Gardnerville.** What a fantastic crowd!
Everywhere I travel, I meet Nevadans who are energized, engaged, and fighting to prevent California ideas from taking over Nevada.
I'm especially grateful for the overwhelming support from Nevadans who believe, as I do, that the State Treasurer's Office should be a place of transparency, accountability, and fiscal responsibility.
**Your money deserves a watchdog!**
But here's the thing: **All the enthusiasm in the world won't matter if we don't turn it into votes.**
We've worked too hard, and there's simply too much at stake, to leave anything to chance.
---
| |

## Make Your Plan to Vote
---
| |
**Early Voting: October 17–30****Election Day: Tuesday, November 3**
Please don't wait until the last minute. Vote early, encourage others to do the same, and help us carry this momentum all the way through Election Day.
I'm incredibly optimistic about what we can accomplish together. But winning requires every one of us to do our part.
**Let's finish strong. Let's get out the vote. And let's win this for Nevada!**
Thank you for standing with me,Drew

I know your inbox is full of campaigns asking for money. Mine is too. So before I ask again, I want to take a minute to explain why my team and I keep doing it, and why your donation matters right now.
**Tonight, my opponent Andy Barr and I are taking the debate stage. Despite him skipping our first debate, we 're still tied.**
The truth is, these asks are a big part of how I will inch ahead in this race. That may sound like a stretch, but hear me out.
In the primary this spring, we were outspent nearly four to one. We won anyway, because thousands of people heard my message and chipped in a few dollars at a time.
Our average donation is $28. That isn't a slogan. _It 's the reason I'm still standing._
Now, Andy Barr has a super PAC that has raised more than $11 million to help him, plus an AI-industry PAC spending to put him in the Senate. We will never match that dollar for dollar. People-powered support is the only way a campaign like ours competes.
Here's what that support turns into. The money that comes in through posts like this one decides how many doors we knock, how many ads we run, and how many Kentuckians we reach before early voting opens on October 29.
So I mean it when I say your grassroots donations can make or break this campaign.
**Before Andy and I debate tomorrow, I need to deliver a resounding blow to his campaign. Can you help me prove the strength of this people-first campaign by chipping in whatever you can spare today?**
[ Chip in to my Senate Campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/09b1c850-5db4-40b9-9797-270f77e08277?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Make a recurring donation](https://substack.com/redirect/df52bbd7-c9cf-4992-a61e-0b2a36b80ffc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you.

Charles Booker

clean_body: This ratings change is happening for two major reasons... | Fellow Patriot, I didn't want to send you this headline. But with 15 days to go, you need to know where this race stands right now. Sabato's Crystal Ball just moved our race from Safe to Likely Republican. This race is tied. And early voting is already underway. Every day we aren't on the air, South Carolinians are casting ballots after hearing only her side of the story. This seat is "at risk." I need to make sure voters hear directly from me, Fellow Patriot. That means a coordinated plan to launch television and digital ads and reach out to voters now that early voting is happening in South Carolina. Annie Andrews has a cash advantage. She's been in this race much longer than we have, and she has the backing of Hollywood's biggest names: Carole King, Mark Hamill, and John Goodman. | | Peter, I need to start this by saying thank you.

I know there’s a lot of campaigns out there – so you opening _this_ email and caring about _this_ movement means the world to me. I _literally_ wouldn’t be in this position without people like you.

As the first Gen Z member of Congress, it's an honor to represent and fight for my generation, at a time when our futures hang in the balance.

This campaign has never been about just me. It’s about all of us. That’s why my campaign is working non-stop to turn out young, new voters, and secure Democratic wins up and down the ballot.

But look, Florida Republicans aren’t messing around. They’re going all out to stop us so they can stay in power. We need to go even harder, but we can’t do that without you.

**So today, I’m asking you for $1. Seriously. Just a dollar.**

I hate asking but there’s too much on the line - _keeping ICE out of our communities, lowering costs for working people, and taking the majority back from the Republicans screwing us over_ \- to just give up now.

A mindblowing 134,820 people have already donated to this campaign. If everyone reading this chipped in **just $1 as their very first contribution to my campaign** , we’d crush our midnight fundraising goal and have the resources we need to out-organize these fascists.

Hi team,
Last week, I went to a very conservative event in Berks County.
**I was the only Democrat in the room.**
And yet, it was clear how much we agree on - we need to lower costs, we're tired of congressional stock trading and feeling like people in Washington fight for their own bottom line, not ours, and we need to come together.
**People are tired of being divided. We 're ready for change. That's why we're going to keep showing up and talking to **_**everyone**_**.**
We're going to get our message out there and make sure our part of PA knows that we have the chance to send someone who fights for _us_ to Congress.
**We 're going to do that tonight at our town hall. We're going to do it tomorrow on the debate stage. And we're going to do it every single one of these next 15 days.**
That's how we're going to win this. But I need you to be a part of it.

body:
[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20261019_partner_ms_aes_em_leftnet.qZeX9K&refcode=em20261019-1721&amount=5&t=1001&akid=1721%2E2118727%2E_WQpwq ][IMG]

If you’ve been keeping an eye on the fight to retake a Democratic majority
in the Senate, you probably already know that competitive seats in states
like Maine, Texas, and Alaska are currently in play for Democrats. That is
massively exciting news.

But as much as I want Democrats to win those races, we have to be
realistic about the math. The fact of the matter is that Republicans only
need to flip Michigan in order to hold onto their majority.

If they flip this seat in Michigan, our chances at winning the Senate are
toast.

I don’t say all this to scare you, but I want to be honest about what this
means for our race:

* Republicans have made me their #1 target to beat in November, and they
are dropping $1 million a day on ads from now until Election Day.

* That means the hundreds of thousands of Michiganders who are currently
choosing whether to vote for me, Mike Rogers, or whether to even vote
at all are being swamped with attack ads in this final push.

# Kern County Farm Bureau Endorses Magsig for Senate
---
|
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** October 19th, 2026Contact: nathan@nathanmagsig.com
---
| | | | | |
**FRESNO, CA** – Nathan Magsig, candidate for California State Senate District 12, announced today that he has received the endorsement of the Kern County Farm Bureau, a leading advocate for the farmers and ranchers who drive the Central Valley's agricultural economy.
"I am honored to have the support of the Kern County Farm Bureau and the hardworking farmers they represent," said Magsig. "Agriculture is the backbone of our Central Valley economy, but Sacramento continues to burden our farmers with unreliable water supplies, skyrocketing energy costs, and excessive regulations. In the State Senate, I will fight to protect our water, lower costs, and make sure the men and women who feed our nation have a strong voice in Sacramento.”
As a Fresno County Supervisor, Magsig has championed policies that support agriculture, strengthen local economies, and protect private property rights. The endorsement adds to his growing coalition of support from organizations and community leaders throughout the Central Valley.
View the full list of endorsements [HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/97OxGf6bSdE?e=6cdbd718cb&c2id=242d1e6b50997e85d906033c0ea9ea06)
---
| | ###
Nathan Magsig is a current Fresno County Supervisor, former Mayor of Clovis, and is running for the 12th Senate District. His family, wife Julie and their three children, reside in Clovis, CA.

# **Treasury identifies $270M in suspected student aid fraud**
The Treasury Department's FinCEN **[flagged roughly $270 million in suspicious activity](https://substack.com/redirect/e96518c9-bbe5-4805-b7d0-b38d66415081?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** tied to possible fraud targeting federal student aid programs, referring the findings to federal investigators for further review.
* **The fraud reportedly involves schemes using stolen identities to create "ghost students"** who fraudulently enroll to claim aid funds, a tactic FinCEN warned financial institutions about in July, noting it can also disadvantage legitimate students trying to enroll.
* **Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration won 't tolerate fraud exploiting government programs,** citing broader efforts including recovering $175 million in erroneous payments to deceased individuals, sanctioning overseas scam networks, and expanding whistleblower tip programs with cash rewards.

# **Feds arrest dozens in California illegal voting crackdown**

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/75ddba47-1680-4bca-8bc3-025d1541258e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Weber pushed back, accusing the DOJ of unlawfully seeking voter data** and sowing distrust, while maintaining California already has safeguards preventing noncitizen registration. Federal prosecutor Bill Essayli said the arrests confirm earlier warnings that noncitizens were voting in the state.

As a reminder, Katy’s opponent, Brandon Herrera, is a pro-gun YouTuber and gun manufacturer. This district includes Uvalde, home to Robb Elementary School – where 19 students and 2 teachers were killed, and 18 were injured by a mass shooter in 2022.

Herrera has stated that the only reason he is in the race is that the congressman representing this district at the time responded to the Uvalde atrocity by voting _in favor_ of a common-sense gun safety bill – the 2022 Safer Communities Act, which expanded background checks and helped states implement red flag laws.

**It gets worse:**

❌ Herrera has worked with Kyle Rittenhouse (who, at 17, shot three men, two fatally, during protests in Wisconsin) to produce a pro-gun video for the National Association for Gun Rights.

❌ He has discussed his copy of Adolf Hitler’s “Mein Kampf,” and used a WWII German weapon, and called it "the original ghetto blaster.”

❌ He has been a member of a white supremacy organization called Sons of Confederate Veterans since he was 12 years old.

❌ He said the following about Shannon Watts, Founder of Moms Demand Action: “Just because you let somebody creampie you, doesn’t mean I have to give a sh*t about your political opinions.” He then went on to refer to children as “c*m trophies."

Despite all of that, and more, when he ran in the Republican primary, he only lost by 1 point.

**This district is extremely winnable for a Democrat – especially now that it’s an open seat. This congressional seat has only ever been held by men, and now would be the perfect time to shatter this glass ceiling while keeping Americans safe from this gun-crazed, hateful YouTuber.**

[**Katy Padilla Stout is a mother and former teacher who supports Red Flag laws and protections. She is ready to fight for children and families. We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines in this race. Help us ensure Katy has what she needs to defeat her neo-Nazi opponent on Election Day by rushing a split $15 or more immediately.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hbm-stout/?refcode=EM_F_261019right_N_BZ_IN_15_G_N_L2&amount=15)

body:
Here’s the full statement from President Obama. It’s worth reading:
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2541%2E791427%2ECn3CfU)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dhs-oct26.4A7Axt&refcode=em261019-1-210&t=2&akid=2541%2E791427%2ECn3CfU)
Friend, I’m grateful to President Obama for drawing this important line in the sand and raising the alarm about Trump’s gross abuse of power.
[**I want to share President Obama’s entire statement with you, but first, please consider chipping in to my campaign today as we organize to fight back against Trump’s corruption and defeat MAGA on November 3rd. Otherwise, please read on:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dhs-oct26.4A7Axt&refcode=em261019-1-210&t=3&akid=2541%2E791427%2ECn3CfU)
**[DONATE HERE](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dhs-oct26.4A7Axt&refcode=em261019-1-210&t=4&akid=2541%2E791427%2ECn3CfU)**
Here’s the full statement from President Obama. It’s worth reading:
“It is a basic principle of American democracy that the government can’t selectively target individuals simply because of their political beliefs or what they say. But that’s exactly what the Trump Administration is doing to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota.”
“To understand why this is so appalling, it’s important to know the facts. Congresswoman Omar came to this country with her father when she was 12 years old. Five years later, her father became a naturalized citizen. If Ilhan had been 18 at the time, she would have had to apply for citizenship separately. But because she was 17, she became a naturalized citizen automatically.”
“Congresswoman Omar went on to graduate from college, work as a community organizer, become the first Somali-American legislator elected to public office in the U.S., and win a seat in Congress. There, she has been one of the Trump Administration’s fiercest critics, which has led the president to repeatedly single her out as someone who he believes does not belong in this country.”
“Now the Administration is actively trying to deport Congresswoman Omar, seemingly based solely on the unsubstantiated theory that she was actually 18 when her father was naturalized, and therefore is not a citizen. Federal agents have raided her home, confiscated personal records, and seized her phone — all to try and uncover a nonexistent smoking gun from 20 years ago that will somehow make their case.”
“Think about that. The full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president. And it’s not the first time this has happened. Under President Trump, the Justice Department has repeatedly gone after those he considers his political enemies — from the Attorney General of New York, to the former head of the FBI, to members of the Federal Reserve.”
“In those cases, the prosecutions either stalled or were dismissed for having no basis in law, and the same is likely to happen in this case. But not before Congresswoman Omar’s life has been turned upside down, her legal bills have piled up, and she’s been forced to spend time fighting unsubstantiated charges instead of serving the people of Minnesota.”
“The fact that any president, or any administration, is willing to engage in such transparent efforts to intimidate someone should outrage all Americans, regardless of how they feel about Congresswoman Omar’s political views. Because if this becomes the new normal, there’s no reason to believe it will stop with her — or that future presidents, in either party, won’t do the same.”
[**Obama is right — we can’t let this authoritarianism become the new normal. Please, consider chipping in to my campaign today and stand with me as I fight back. We are in a struggle for the future of our democracy, our civil rights, and the working class, and we must win.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dhs-oct26.4A7Axt&refcode=em261019-1-210&t=5&akid=2541%2E791427%2ECn3CfU)

Here’s the full statement from President Obama. Congresswoman Omar came to this country with her father when she was 12 years old. Five years later, her father became a naturalized citizen. If Ilhan had been 18 at the time, she would have had to apply for citizenship separately. But because she was 17, she became a naturalized citizen automatically.” “Congresswoman Omar went on to graduate from college, work as a community organizer, become the first Somali-American legislator elected to public office in the U.S., and win a seat in Congress. There, she has been one of the Trump Administration’s fiercest critics, which has led the president to repeatedly single her out as someone who he believes does not belong in this country.” “Now the Administration is actively trying to deport Congresswoman Omar, seemingly based solely on the unsubstantiated theory that she was actually 18 when her father was naturalized, and therefore is not a citizen. Charlie said it best in the days leading up to President Trump's victory in 2024: _" I don't care about polls. __ __I don 't care about betting markets. __ __I don 't care about vibes. __ _ **_I care about how many ballots are in the box. _**_ __If we turnout, we win. __ _**_Do the work. clean_body: So much is on our ballot | | | | = | | | Election Day is in 15 days, and so much is on the line across our Commonwealth. We have competitive U.S. House races, an important Senate contest, and three consequential amendments before voters. We need Virginians to show up and vote YES on all 3 amendments! Each choice will shape our future in a different way, but every one of them depends on Virginians knowing what is at stake and showing up to vote. = = Our work is statewide because our values are statewide: strong public schools, affordable healthcare, reproductive freedom, economic opportunity, and a government that reflects the people it serves. In these final 15 days, we are supporting the conversations and grassroots energy that can carry those values to the ballot box. There is no shortcut to turnout. It takes volunteers, trusted messengers, and the resources to reach people where they are. It also takes clear information, repeated reminders, and neighbors willing to speak with neighbors. The choices are on the ballot; our responsibility is to make sure Virginians in every region make their voices heard. = | | | = With gratitude, Ghazala Hashmi= = | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- | | | Email us: info@nextchapterpac.org This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Team,

I'm often asked why I didn't wait my turn — why a first-time congressional candidate would take on a 21-year incumbent instead of waiting for a seat to open up.

My answer is always the same: We don't have the luxury of waiting.

We can't wait while families are being separated by ICE.

We can't wait while people in the richest country in the world are forced to choose between putting food on the table and getting the healthcare they need.

We can't wait while housing costs push working families further to the brink every single month.

And we can't wait for a new generation of leadership that will actually fight for working people — because that moment is right now.

This race was never just about one congressional seat. It's about whether we settle for business as usual, or finally demand something better.

But here's what we're up against, and why I'm writing you today. The outside money trying to stop this movement is piling up fast. In just the last two days, super PAC attacks against us have jumped from $1 million to over $1.5 million — and it's still climbing.

**[So I'm asking you not to wait until it's too late to make an impact. With ballots already in voters' hands, every day matters. Mai is the daughter of Hmong refugees, born and raised in Sacramento. Mai’s parents fled war in Laos and arrived in California to find a new life.

As the oldest of 16 children, she helped raise her siblings while working hard to build a career dedicated to helping her community thrive. Mai is a proud product of public schools and was the first in her family to attend college. As a young organizer, Mai returned home to serve the community that raised and supported her.

We are in the final stretch to Election Day — and it's time to organize

In these closing weeks, Our Revolution is mobilizing our people-powered

Task Force to End Corporate Greed and the fight to lower costs for working
families.

grassroots No Kings mobilization to turn out voters and defeat MAGA at the
ballot box.

⭐ Melat Kiros for Congress (CO-01) on her campaign and the opportunity to
bring a new generation of progressive leadership to Congress.

⭐ Randy Villegas for Congress (CA-22) on his campaign to flip a critical
House seat and fight for working families in California’s Central Valley.

⭐ Will Lawrence for Congress (MI-07) on his campaign to flip a key House
seat and fight for economic justice for Michigan families.

⭐ Eli Savit for Michigan Attorney General on the stakes of state-level
races and the importance of electing leaders to hold powerful interests
accountable.

⭐Vikki Goodwin (Texas Lt. Governor) — A four-term progressive state rep
running to fully fund public schools and put Texas families ahead of
corporate interests.

power from the ground up and why down-ballot organizing matters in the
final GOTV sprint.

This year marks 10 years since Bernie Sanders founded Our Revolution.
Since then, we’ve helped elect more than 1,200 progressives — from city

voter turnout machine.

Now, everything we’ve built is being put to work.

possible voter, flip Congress, elect a new wave of progressives, and build
the grassroots power to take on Trump, MAGA, and corporate power.

name: John Thune
subject: Democrats are coming for red states. Montana is next.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alme for Senate
body:
Democrats are flooding red states with outside money. Montana cannot be the one that slips away. |
---
FROM THE DESK OF SENATOR JOHN THUNE:
I want to be direct with you about something I am watching closely.

Democrats are not just playing defense this cycle. They are on offense - targeting red states they have no business competing in, flooding them with outside money, and running candidates specifically designed to fool voters into thinking they are getting a moderate when they are actually getting another loyal Schumer vote.

**Montana is one of those states. But I refuse to let it slip away without a fight.**

**[Peter, that is why I am asking you to stand with Trump-endorsed Kurt Alme today.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=6efc592253494e1c8bc764f7938f5371&_e=fNytn9_l_mXF2fi3ScnaXgmK41jBXq4LQasiPV_0f9hxIjEN40sLDDEvYLrYsTTf-F9NTHoHHotm7nTKmS5AdcxjKInjdFKGXD9i4-d4u1ktI_Rsdabto0yTWa6pMWwY58v7xMjXuTKsMA2V1-Fky3u8Y7EBBauZQZJSljRcczAa4rjP2shRtajQBjt-Txn8aLfzBkyuwa-OU0rrASii-5O-jKZOiNuthuSAOoNAf13CmmNyCvE-Ph2q2HJDQWjkVI22m7ZI4s7p1TyVLHOnY6VhyygJH8PWomAuUQueO83l7U6fI3T6ilTOnEusqZCOxgHwXtXrps3gVHOMMpETBpzyaEXbZYQYi3dcWkryo3BG6gQtO9mbQWX9bbV-N-m59jOzEEtu2SKy8dHKJC7UvAc5EGtJDmsKk84M7xstpR0Rm2xhp0QoREdt4bB9hvBNHHDebOrvAv5lal469Kuvzf9WvHGi3oFzGA2dyZipaU_IvDynkqR4RjX8IAUIkAeALaq2ioJNGXp7dsp2KMK1wsX_ygX8E2If5fGOZkFWfIHKGE0uOjfhcjUIkYoyTNXKpuEhOTyFg4KdccMaZKxZsu3P9ZjOl_r_SmFoVpU0WhR5TXIR4LOLskzT-JFYmfP1mysFYWzFQPq6nYRnkwXljGlXFO8jZJtH5o5i1CkN9juNDxjdmG_TfO6aC7LuT2RlUC-OR09X7Iu-4l7pHwEz-38i35Ha4JhsXLytdXbY_AE%3D) ** [**STAND WITH KURT >>**](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=6efc592253494e1c8bc764f7938f5371&_e=fNytn9_l_mXF2fi3ScnaXgmK41jBXq4LQasiPV_0f9hxIjEN40sLDDEvYLrYsTTf-F9NTHoHHotm7nTKmS5AdcxjKInjdFKGXD9i4-d4u1ktI_Rsdabto0yTWa6pMWwY58v7xMjXuTKsMA2V1-Fky3u8Y7EBBauZQZJSljRcczAa4rjP2shRtajQBjt-Txn8aLfzBkyuwa-OU0rrASii-5O-jKZOiNuthuSAOoNAf13CmmNyCvE-Ph2q2HJDQWjk3ba5fknzXGrdkFKgaCxGQkh_h2u8QzjhveY4RnzN8TlB1z2ytvJ4FIPkwAhDrT8RAZdlcWskg2s36Lj98SgECIEmEq-d9XpHoB6_x7D58o5LYWtdtS7Dw2yv-Is9A0NIBGT0Ph6LKuxAbGjhBNW4M9dJ_9tUNHswDQOzIH5zQ-wN6z4haGs-TixzzwWWLwOWD49FcV2Z56ud0qyhUjVXcjGS8LzxiSI3qqK0ms7kMNl7tJ1TDbN622ADPgFOx-Fwn-PcusmrNE27fU5pB9fFkt4ytgtAdOptZdkemijLznAW6GpIq2r2m385RpnTQXDKQS-TrzP-oQfxN2zD3vFbwiIit_hOc8foWHkzJxXvTdK5bP9rwcTh5WfCbQNOS5mLPGzuLxvpI10doLOuBPY6g_D8JDgwG9yx4MuoAolaGnr7p3HZ7a56kg6EC4Ek6XuvOcbPY0TF52wPyo9zNllVH0L1WVahCPsBmkerNRRH6JI%3D)
I have served in the Senate long enough to know how these races unfold. Democrats identify a target, recruit a candidate, and pour in millions of dollars before the Republican side has had time to build. By the time conservatives see what is happening, the gap is already significant.

I refuse to let that happen here.

Kurt Alme is exactly the kind of candidate Montana needs - a Trump-nominated federal prosecutor with a real record of results. He took on cartels, drug traffickers, and violent criminals as U.S. attorney. He cut Montana's income tax rate. He helped make Montana debt-free. **_He has President Trump's complete and total endorsement, and mine._**

But here is the reality. Schumer has two candidates in this race, both funded by out-of-state money, both running the same bait-and-switch playbook we have seen in state after state. They are not running to represent Montana. They are running to give the Senate back to Chuck Schumer.

Peter, maintaining our Senate Republican Majority is not just about this seat - it is about our ability to confirm conservative judges, advance President Trump's agenda, and provide a check on Washington's excesses. _Every seat matters. This one especially._

body:
This time it's a Senate candidate. Their deadline is tomorrow, and we're not backing down.
